sentences.text: Purpose: Normative design contract for architecture, RTL, verification, DFT, and physical integration of this IP.
Status of this draft: All design decisions DEC-001 to DEC-047 are closed (Section 20.2).
No (DEC-xxx) reference marks an open point; the references show where a decision acts.
DEC-025 to DEC-036 belong to the software reset (FEAT-012, Section 10.7): the requester chose the active-low input i_rst_n_sw and accepted the author's proposals for the other eleven points.

The few values chosen by the author on the requester's delegation or as a proposal accepted by the requester are recorded in Section 20.2 (for example the plusarg names, the default seed, the example cell and macro models).
Section 20.3 lists the open decisions: none.
Requirement terms: shall = mandatory and testable; should = recommended; may = optional.

The IP transfers a stream of data words from a write clock domain to an unrelated read clock domain.
Words are read in the order they were written.
The write and read pointers cross the domains as Gray codes through configurable synchronizers.
The IP reports full, empty, threshold, overflow, and underflow conditions to the two domains.
Included:
Structural top m_vlsit_afifo_top that instantiates the write module, the read module, and the FIFO array module.
Write module (write clock domain), read module (read clock domain).

Synchronizer module that instantiates one technology cell wrapper per bit, with five cell options (bypass, two D flip-flop cells, a 2-FF, a 3-FF or a 4-FF cell), a configurable bit width, and a configurable reset value.
It is the only module that instantiates the cell wrapper, and the wrapper is the only module with cells and the metastability model.
FIFO array module with a pure RTL implementation and a library SRAM (one write port, one read port) replacement branch.
Flags: full, empty, full with threshold, empty with threshold, overflow, underflow.
Software reset: a reset input in the write clock domain with a four-phase handshake that resets both pointers in the right order and blocks both interfaces during the reset (Section 10.7).
Verification-only models: synchronizer metastability model and SRAM macro model.
Example technology cell models (no library cell is available; Section 14.4).
Excluded:
Reset synchronizers.
Each reset input is already synchronized to its own clock (REQ-RESET-001).
Clock generation, clock gating, and clock-ratio control.
Software-visible registers and the CSR workbook (N/A, DEC-003 closed).
ECC or parity of stored data.
Any data width conversion or multi-word transaction protocol.

Item: Operating modes and workload; Specification: Two asynchronous clocks. There is no restriction on the frequency or the frequency ratio (DEC-009)
Item: Security / privilege context; Specification: None (Section 18)
Item: External dependencies; Specification: Clock and reset sources of both domains, library synchronizer cell (optional), library SRAM macro (optional)

REF-003 is the mandatory RTL baseline.
A requirement that conflicts with REF-003 is not accepted; it is listed as a decision instead of a local exception.
The simulation models are outside the RTL rules (DEC-001).
This specification defines the IP contract and shall stay consistent with REF-002 and REF-003.
No CSR is specified in this document.

Naming of modules, ports, signals, and parameters follows REF-003 Section 2 with the project prefixes m_vlsit_afifo_, PARA_AFIFO_.

ID: REQ-FUNC-001; Requirement using shall/should/may: The IP shall implement an asynchronous FIFO with an independent write clock domain and read clock domain.; Source: REF-002; Applies to: All; Verification method: SIM

ID: REQ-FUNC-002; Requirement using shall/should/may: The pointers shall cross between the two domains as Gray codes only. Each Gray pointer register shall change at most one bit per clock cycle of its own domain.; Source: REF-002; Applies to: All; Verification method: FRM, SIM

ID: REQ-FUNC-003; Requirement using shall/should/may: Words shall be read in the order they were written. Every accepted write shall be read exactly once. No word shall be lost, duplicated, or reordered.; Source: REF-002; Applies to: All; Verification method: SIM, FRM

ID: REQ-FUNC-004; Requirement using shall/should/may: A write shall be accepted at a write-clock edge when i_wr_en = 1 and the full flag is 0. It shall store i_wr_data in the entry addressed by the write pointer and advance the write pointer by one.; Source: REF-002; Applies to: All; Verification method: SIM

ID: REQ-FUNC-005; Requirement using shall/should/may: A read shall be accepted at a read-clock edge when i_rd_en = 1 and the empty flag is 0. It shall advance the read pointer by one. The read data interface is show-ahead (REQ-FUNC-017).; Source: REF-002; Applies to: All; Verification method: SIM

ID: REQ-FUNC-006; Requirement using shall/should/may: Each domain shall hold a binary pointer of LPARA_PTR_W = log2(depth) + 1 bits and a Gray pointer register derived from the next binary pointer. The Gray pointer register is the launch register of the crossing (no logic between it and the synchronizer).; Source: REF-002, REF-003 CLK-01; Applies to: All; Verification method: INS, CDC

ID: REQ-FUNC-007; Requirement using shall/should/may: The depth shall be a power of 2, because a Gray pointer wraps with a one-bit change only for a power-of-2 range. Minimum depth is 2. There is no upper limit on the depth (DEC-004).; Source: Architecture; Applies to: All; Verification method: LNT, SIM

ID: REQ-FUNC-008; Requirement using shall/should/may: The full flag is generated in the write domain. It shall be 1 whenever the write domain has no free entry, judged from the synchronized read pointer. It shall never be 0 while the FIFO is physically full. It may stay 1 late after a read frees an entry (pessimistic).; Source: REF-002; Applies to: All; Verification method: FRM, SIM

ID: REQ-FUNC-009; Requirement using shall/should/may: The empty flag is generated in the read domain. It shall be 1 whenever the read domain has no word to read, judged from the synchronized write pointer. It shall never be 0 while the FIFO is physically empty. It may stay 1 late after a write (pessimistic).; Source: REF-002; Applies to: All; Verification method: FRM, SIM

ID: REQ-FUNC-010; Requirement using shall/should/may: The IP shall provide o_full_thr (write domain) and o_empty_thr (read domain), each with its own threshold input. o_full_thr shall be 1 when the write-domain occupancy estimate is greater than or equal to i_full_thr. o_empty_thr shall be 1 when the read-domain occupancy estimate is less than or equal to i_empty_thr. The occupancy estimate is the binary write pointer minus the binary read pointer, where the pointer of the other domain is the synchronized one (Section 9); it is pessimistic for the full side (it can be larger than the true occupancy) and for the empty side (it can be smaller). Both flags are combinational. The thresholds are static: they are written once before the FIFO is used and do not change while it is in use. Every value of LPARA_PTR_W bits is accepted; the comparisons are defined for all of them (for example i_full_thr = 0 makes o_full_thr always 1, and a value above the depth makes it never 1).; Source: Requester; Applies to: All; Verification method: SIM

ID: REQ-FUNC-011; Requirement using shall/should/may: m_vlsit_afifo_top shall be a structural wrapper that instantiates only m_vlsit_afifo_wr, m_vlsit_afifo_rd, and m_vlsit_afifo_mem.; Source: Requester (DEC-014), REF-003 HIE-02; Applies to: All; Verification method: INS

ID: REQ-FUNC-012; Requirement using shall/should/may: m_vlsit_afifo_wr shall contain the write pointer logic, the full and threshold logic, the overflow logic, the synchronizer of the read Gray pointer, the write-side software reset FSM and the synchronizer of the acknowledge, and the memory write port outputs. m_vlsit_afifo_rd shall contain the read pointer logic, the empty and threshold logic, the underflow logic, and the synchronizer of the write Gray pointer, the read-side software reset FSM and the synchronizer of the request, and the memory read address output.; Source: REF-002; Applies to: All; Verification method: INS

ID: REQ-FUNC-013; Requirement using shall/should/may: m_vlsit_afifo_sync shall provide a synchronizer with a configurable bit width and a reset value for every bit. The number of stages is set by PARA_AFIFO_CELL_TYPE: 2 stages for the options 1 and 2, 3 for the option 3, 4 for the option 4 (S in Section 10.3), and 0 for the option 0 (bypass, DEC-039).; Source: REF-002, Requester (DEC-039); Applies to: All; Verification method: SIM, LNT

ID: REQ-FUNC-014; Requirement using shall/should/may: m_vlsit_afifo_sync shall contain no flip-flop, cell, or model of its own: it shall instantiate only the wrapper m_vlsit_afifo_cell_sync, one wrapper per synchronized bit, in every configuration and in both branches of the macro VLSIT_SYNTHESIS (DEC-039). The wrapper shall select the cell by the parameter PARA_AFIFO_CELL_TYPE (DEC-037): 0 = bypass (o_q = i_d, no cell, no stage); 1 = two D flip-flop cells in series (2 stages); 2 = one 2-FF synchronizer cell (2 stages); 3 = one 3-FF synchronizer cell (3 stages); 4 = one 4-FF synchronizer cell (4 stages). Option 0 has no synchronization: it is not a legal choice for a Gray pointer crossing (Section 14.4).; Source: REF-002, REF-003 HIE-07, Requester (DEC-037, DEC-039); Applies to: All; Verification method: INS, LNT, SIM

ID: REQ-FUNC-015; Requirement using shall/should/may: m_vlsit_afifo_mem shall be an independent module instantiated in m_vlsit_afifo_top. It shall be modelled as an SRAM with one write port (write clock domain) and one read port (read clock domain), so that it can be replaced by an ASIC library SRAM macro.; Source: Requester (DEC-014); Applies to: All; Verification method: INS

ID: REQ-FUNC-016; Requirement using shall/should/may: m_vlsit_afifo_mem shall provide a generate branch that replaces the pure RTL array with a library SRAM that has one write port and one read port, through the wrapper m_vlsit_afifo_ram_macro. The default is the pure RTL array.; Source: REF-002, REF-003 HIE-06, HIE-07; Applies to: All; Verification method: INS, SIM

ID: REQ-FUNC-017; Requirement using shall/should/may: o_rd_data shall always show the word stored at the current read pointer, including while the FIFO is empty (show-ahead). It is the output of the synchronous storage read port: the read module drives the address of the next read pointer (the current read pointer, plus one if a read is accepted in this cycle) and the storage is read in every read-clock cycle, so after each read-clock edge o_rd_data is the word at the new read pointer. While empty or before the entry was ever written, its value is the storage content, which is undefined. There is no o_rd_valid; validity is o_empty = 0.; Source: Requester (DEC-005, DEC-022); Applies to: All; Verification method: SIM

ID: REQ-FUNC-018; Requirement using shall/should/may: The full, empty, full-with-threshold, and empty-with-threshold flags shall be combinational functions of the local pointer registers and the synchronized pointer of the other domain.; Source: Requester (DEC-016); Applies to: All; Verification method: SIM, FRM

ID: REQ-IF-001; Requirement using shall/should/may: The ports of every module shall be as listed in Section 6. The top ports do not depend on the parameter values.; Source: REF-003 PRT-03; Applies to: All; Verification method: LNT

ID: REQ-CLK-001; Requirement using shall/should/may: The write and read clocks shall be treated as fully asynchronous. The IP shall not assume a phase or frequency relation. There is no restriction on the frequency or on the frequency ratio (DEC-009).; Source: REF-002; Applies to: All; Verification method: CDC, SIM

ID: REQ-CLK-002; Requirement using shall/should/may: Every clock-domain crossing shall use a Gray pointer registered in its own domain, followed directly by m_vlsit_afifo_sync in the destination domain, with no logic before the first stage or between stages.; Source: REF-003 CLK-01, P28; Applies to: All; Verification method: CDC, INS

ID: REQ-CLK-003; Requirement using shall/should/may: The read data path from the FIFO array (write-domain storage) to the read domain shall be valid whenever the pointer protocol of Section 10.4 allows a read.; Source: Architecture; Applies to: All; Verification method: SIM, CDC

ID: REQ-CLK-004; Requirement using shall/should/may: m_vlsit_afifo_wr shall contain only logic of the write clock domain, and m_vlsit_afifo_rd shall contain only logic of the read clock domain. The FIFO array is a dual-clock storage owned by neither half; it is instantiated in the top (DEC-014).; Source: Requester; Applies to: All; Verification method: INS, CDC

ID: REQ-RESET-001; Requirement using shall/should/may: i_rst_n_wr shall be already synchronized to i_clk_wr and i_rst_n_rd already synchronized to i_clk_rd. The IP shall not contain a reset synchronizer.; Source: REF-002; Applies to: All; Verification method: INS

ID: REQ-RESET-002; Requirement using shall/should/may: After reset (hardware reset, or the release of a software reset, REQ-SRST-012) the FIFO shall be empty: both pointers 0, full = 0, empty = 1, overflow = 0, underflow = 0. The flops use an asynchronous-assert, active-low reset. The two resets are independent and need not be asserted at the same time (ASM-005).; Source: Requester, Architecture; Applies to: All; Verification method: SIM
ID: REQ-PARAM-001; Requirement using shall/should/may: The number of entries (depth) shall be configurable by PARA_AFIFO_DEPTH.; Source: REF-002; Applies to: All; Verification method: SIM, LNT
ID: REQ-PARAM-002; Requirement using shall/should/may: The data bit width shall be configurable by PARA_AFIFO_DATA_W.; Source: REF-002; Applies to: All; Verification method: SIM, LNT

ID: REQ-PARAM-003; Requirement using shall/should/may: The legal parameter values are those of Section 8. The RTL shall not contain an elaboration check for illegal values (DEC-002); the behavior with an illegal value is undefined, and the verification configurations shall use legal values only.; Source: Requester (DEC-002); Applies to: All; Verification method: LNT

ID: REQ-ERR-001; Requirement using shall/should/may: When a write is requested while the FIFO is full, the overflow flag shall be raised and the write shall not change the stored data or the write pointer. The flag is a 1-cycle pulse (Section 12).; Source: REF-002; Applies to: All; Verification method: SIM, FRM

ID: REQ-ERR-002; Requirement using shall/should/may: When a read is requested while the FIFO is empty, the underflow flag shall be raised and the read shall not change the read pointer. The flag is a 1-cycle pulse (Section 12); o_rd_data keeps showing the word at the current read pointer.; Source: REF-002; Applies to: All; Verification method: SIM, FRM

ID: REQ-SRST-001; Requirement using shall/should/may: The IP shall have the input i_rst_n_sw, an active-low level in the write clock domain (DEC-025). A software reset sequence starts when i_rst_n_sw = 0 is seen at a write-clock edge while the write reset FSM is in RUN. The input may be held for one write-clock cycle or for any longer time (DEC-026).; Source: Requester; Applies to: All; Verification method: SIM, FRM

ID: REQ-SRST-002; Requirement using shall/should/may: The request shall be a register req_wr in m_vlsit_afifo_wr. It shall cross to the read domain through m_vlsit_afifo_sync (width 1, the same stage count as the pointers, CDC-005), with no logic before the first stage.; Source: Requester; Applies to: All; Verification method: CDC, INS

ID: REQ-SRST-003; Requirement using shall/should/may: While the synchronized request is 1, or the read reset FSM is not in RUN, a read request shall not be accepted. The block is combinational (zero latency) from these two conditions.; Source: Requester; Applies to: All; Verification method: SIM, FRM

ID: REQ-SRST-004; Requirement using shall/should/may: From the cycle in which the read side is blocked until the read side is released, o_empty shall be 1.; Source: Requester; Applies to: All; Verification method: SIM

ID: REQ-SRST-005; Requirement using shall/should/may: When the read reset FSM has seen the request, it shall reset the read pointer (binary and Gray) to 0, and only then raise the acknowledge ack_rd (register in m_vlsit_afifo_rd).; Source: Requester; Applies to: All; Verification method: SIM, FRM

ID: REQ-SRST-006; Requirement using shall/should/may: The acknowledge shall cross to the write domain through m_vlsit_afifo_sync (width 1, same stage count, CDC-006), with no logic before the first stage.; Source: Requester; Applies to: All; Verification method: CDC, INS

ID: REQ-SRST-007; Requirement using shall/should/may: When the write reset FSM has seen the synchronized acknowledge, it shall reset the write pointer (binary and Gray) to 0.; Source: Requester; Applies to: All; Verification method: SIM, FRM

ID: REQ-SRST-008; Requirement using shall/should/may: From the write-clock cycle in which i_rst_n_sw = 0, and until the write reset FSM is back in RUN, a write request shall not be accepted. The block is combinational (zero latency) from i_rst_n_sw and the FSM state (DEC-030).; Source: Requester; Applies to: All; Verification method: SIM, FRM

ID: REQ-SRST-009; Requirement using shall/should/may: The handshake shall have four phases: request up, acknowledge up, request down, acknowledge down. The request shall fall only after i_rst_n_sw = 1 and after the write pointer is reset. The acknowledge shall fall only after the request is seen at 0 in the read domain.; Source: Requester; Applies to: All; Verification method: SIM, FRM

ID: REQ-SRST-010; Requirement using shall/should/may: The read reset FSM shall leave its acknowledge state (return to RUN) only when the synchronized request is 0 and the synchronized write Gray pointer is 0. The write reset FSM shall return to RUN only when the synchronized acknowledge is 0 and the synchronized read Gray pointer is 0 (flush check, Section 10.7.3) (DEC-034).; Source: Architecture, simulation evidence of Section 10.7.6; Applies to: All; Verification method: SIM, FRM

ID: REQ-SRST-011; Requirement using shall/should/may: After the software reset, the read side shall be released before the write side: the read FSM returns to RUN before the write FSM returns to RUN.; Source: Requester; Applies to: All; Verification method: SIM, FRM

ID: REQ-SRST-012; Requirement using shall/should/may: After the release, the flags shall be generated by the normal FIFO logic from the pointers. Both pointers are 0, so o_empty = 1 and o_full = 0 until the first write has crossed to the read domain.; Source: Requester; Applies to: All; Verification method: SIM

ID: REQ-SRST-013; Requirement using shall/should/may: The sequence shall complete for any width of i_rst_n_sw (one cycle or more), for any frequency and ratio of the two clocks, and with the metastability model enabled (random extra latency on every crossing).; Source: Requester, architecture; Applies to: All; Verification method: SIM

ID: REQ-SRST-014; Requirement using shall/should/may: The words that are in the FIFO when the software reset starts are discarded. A read accepted before the request reaches the read domain returns a valid pre-reset word. The storage content is not cleared (DEC-035).; Source: Architecture; Applies to: All; Verification method: SIM

ID: REQ-SRST-015; Requirement using shall/should/may: A hardware reset of a domain shall have priority over the software reset: it resets the FSM and the pointers of its domain asynchronously (DEC-031).; Source: Architecture; Applies to: All; Verification method: SIM

ID: REQ-SRST-016; Requirement using shall/should/may: If i_rst_n_sw = 0 is seen again while the write FSM is in REL, writes shall stay blocked and a new sequence shall start when the FSM is back in RUN (DEC-032).; Source: Architecture; Applies to: All; Verification method: SIM

ID: REQ-SRST-017; Requirement using shall/should/may: During the software reset: o_full shall be 1 while the write side is blocked (DEC-027); a blocked write or read shall not raise o_overflow or o_underflow (DEC-028); o_full_thr and o_empty_thr shall take the values of an empty FIFO (DEC-029).; Source: Architecture; Applies to: All; Verification method: SIM

ID: REQ-SRST-018; Requirement using shall/should/may: The output o_sw_rst_busy shall be the output of a dedicated flip-flop reg_sw_rst_busy of m_vlsit_afifo_wr, with no combinational logic between the flop and the port. It shall be set at the write-clock edge where the write reset FSM leaves RUN (the first edge at which the FSM takes the request) and cleared at the write-clock edge where it returns to RUN. It shall therefore be 1 in the states REQ, PTR, HOLD, and REL and 0 in RUN, at every write-clock edge, independently of the level of i_rst_n_sw and of the state of the read reset FSM. It shall be 0 after the hardware reset i_rst_n_wr (asynchronous clear). The write block is wr_blk = o_sw_rst_busy OR (i_rst_n_sw = 0).; Source: Requester; Applies to: All; Verification method: SIM, FRM, INS

ID: REQ-RTL-001; Requirement using shall/should/may: The RTL shall comply with REF-003. Technology cells and memory macros shall appear only in the dedicated wrappers m_vlsit_afifo_cell_sync and m_vlsit_afifo_ram_macro.; Source: REF-003; Applies to: All; Verification method: LNT, INS

ID: REQ-RTL-002; Requirement using shall/should/may: The synthesis, lint, CDC, formal, and equivalence flows shall define the macro VLSIT_SYNTHESIS. In the branch selected by this macro, m_vlsit_afifo_cell_sync contains only instances of the library cells and follows REF-003. The branch of this module without the macro is simulation-only and is excluded from REF-003 (DEC-001, DEC-021). m_vlsit_afifo_sync and m_vlsit_afifo_ram_macro have a single branch and follow REF-003 in every flow (DEC-039, DEC-043). A simulation that defines VLSIT_SYNTHESIS runs the synthesizable branches.; Source: Requester (DEC-021); Applies to: All; Verification method: LNT, INS

ID: REQ-RTL-003; Requirement using shall/should/may: The instance of every technology library cell and memory macro shall be named u_dont_touch_ (rule R-028, REF-003 NAM-09): u_dont_touch_dff_0, u_dont_touch_dff_1, u_dont_touch_sync2ff, u_dont_touch_sync3ff, u_dont_touch_sync4ff, u_dont_touch_sram. Instances of design modules keep u_.; Source: Requester; Applies to: All; Verification method: LNT, INS

ID: REQ-VER-001; Requirement using shall/should/may: m_vlsit_afifo_cell_sync shall contain a simulation model of the metastability of the synchronizer in the branch that is compiled when the macro VLSIT_SYNTHESIS is not defined (DEC-021, DEC-038). The wrapper is one bit, so every bit of a synchronizer is modelled independently; the model applies to the options 1 to 4 of PARA_AFIFO_CELL_TYPE (N = 2, 2, 3, 4 stages, the number S below is N), and the option 0 (bypass) has no stage and no model. No other module models metastability: m_vlsit_afifo_sync only instantiates m_vlsit_afifo_cell_sync for every bit, and the other modules only instantiate m_vlsit_afifo_sync (DEC-039). For every bit, when the input changes value, the model shall apply a random latency, chosen independently for each bit and each change. The latency is counted in destination clock cycles after the first capturing edge: the nominal value of an S-stage synchronizer is S-1 and the model adds 0, 1, or 2 extra cycles, so the latency is S-1, S, or S+1 (1, 2, 3 for S = 2; 2, 3, 4 for S = 3; 3, 4, 5 for S = 4). Counted in edges from the input change, with the first edge after the change as edge 1, the output changes at edge S, S+1, or S+2. If the input changes again during the delay, the new value replaces the pending change and the delay restarts. The model is written in professional SystemVerilog, is not bound by the RTL rules of REF-003, and is never used for synthesis (DEC-001). Write: the write domain accepts i_wr_data when i_wr_en = 1 and full = 0.
The write module drives the memory write port of m_vlsit_afifo_mem (enable, address = low LPARA_ADDR_W bits of the binary write pointer, data), which stores the word.
The binary pointer is incremented, its Gray code is registered, and the Gray pointer crosses to the read domain (CDC-001).
Visibility: after S read-clock stages (S = stages of the selected cell, Section 10.3) the read domain sees the new write Gray pointer.
Empty is updated from it.
Read: o_rd_data always shows the word at the read address (show-ahead).
The read domain accepts a read when i_rd_en = 1 and empty = 0.
It increments the read pointer, so o_rd_data then shows the next word, and registers the Gray code.
The Gray pointer crosses to the write domain (CDC-002).
Release: after the synchronizer latency the write domain sees the new read pointer.
Full is updated and the entry is available for a new write.

Software reset: i_rst_n_sw starts a handshake between the two domains that blocks both interfaces, resets the read pointer first and the write pointer after the acknowledge, and releases the read side before the write side (Section 10.7).
The read data crosses from the write-domain storage to the read domain without a synchronizer (CDC-003).
It is safe because an entry is read only after its write pointer has been seen by the read domain, and it is overwritten only after its read pointer has been seen by the write domain.
The storage read port is synchronous and is read every read-clock cycle (DEC-022).
The storage output register of the read domain can capture an unsettled word only while the FIFO is empty, and the word is captured again before o_empty falls (Section 10.4).
The array module is instantiated in the top (DEC-014).
Its write port is driven by the write module with write-domain signals, and its read port by the read module with read-domain signals.
The array is a dual-clock storage that belongs to neither half, so REQ-CLK-004 applies to the write and read modules only.
The read data returns to the read module.
INV-001: the number of stored words (write pointer minus read pointer, modulo 2 x depth) is between 0 and PARA_AFIFO_DEPTH.
INV-002: full and empty are never both 1 (depth >= 1).
INV-003: a Gray pointer register changes at most one bit per clock cycle.
INV-004: the write side never overwrites an entry that is not yet read; the read side never reads an entry that is not yet written (from the point of view of the registered flags).
INV-005: a rejected write (overflow) and a rejected read (underflow) leave pointers and storage unchanged.
INV-006: at the instant a side leaves the software reset, its own pointer and its synchronized copy of the other pointer are both 0.
The read side leaves the software reset before the write side.

Type: CLK; Meaning: Clock; What the user shall know: Free running, rising edge active. No gating inside the IP

Type: RST-L; Meaning: Reset level, active-low; What the user shall know: A level (not a pulse). Asserted asynchronously, de-asserted synchronously to the clock of its domain, already synchronized outside the IP. It shall stay low for at least one clock edge of its domain so that the flops are reset

Type: LVL-REQ; Meaning: Request level, active-high; What the user shall know: A level sampled at every rising edge of its clock. It may stay 1 for many cycles. Each edge at which it is 1 and the acceptance condition holds is one transaction (one word). It is not edge-detected and has no minimum width: hold it for as many cycles as words are wanted

Type: LVL-DATA; Meaning: Data level; What the user shall know: A bus that is sampled only at an edge where the matching LVL-REQ is accepted (write data), or that shows a value continuously (read data). No handshake, no hold requirement after the sampling edge

Type: LVL-STS; Meaning: Status level; What the user shall know: A flag computed combinationally from registers. It is 1 for as long as the condition holds, not just for one cycle. It changes after a clock edge (or after a synchronizer stage), never between edges except for the effect of the static thresholds

Type: REG-STS; Meaning: Registered status level; What the user shall know: The output of a flip-flop, with no combinational logic between the flop and the port. It changes only at a clock edge of its domain and holds its value until the next event

Type: PULSE; Meaning: Registered event pulse; What the user shall know: Output of a flop. One pulse cycle per event: it is 1 for exactly one clock period after the edge that carried the event, and returns to 0 by itself. It is not sticky. If events happen in consecutive cycles, the output stays 1 for as many consecutive cycles (one cycle per event). The consumer shall sample it at every clock edge or count the cycles

Type: STATIC; Meaning: Quasi-static level; What the user shall know: A configuration value written once, before the FIFO is used, and not changed while the FIFO is in use. No synchronizer, no clock domain (false path, CDC-004)

Type: LVL-CTL; Meaning: Control level (the active polarity is stated for each port); What the user shall know: A level sampled at every rising edge. The IP reacts to the level, not to an edge. It may be asserted for one cycle or for any longer time. One reset sequence is run for one assertion; the sequence ends only after the level is de-asserted again

Type: REG-LVL; Meaning: Registered level, internal; What the user shall know: A flop output that crosses to the other domain through a 1-bit synchronizer. It changes only on a handshake step and stays stable until the other side has answered

Type: REG-GRAY; Meaning: Registered level, internal; What the user shall know: The Gray pointer register output. Changes by one bit at most at a clock edge. Crosses to the other domain through the synchronizer of that domain
Type: INT; Meaning: Internal level; What the user shall know: Combinational or registered interconnect between two blocks of the IP

Port: i_clk_wr; Dir: Input; Width: 1; Type: CLK; Function: Write clock (macro CLKW); Active: Rising edge
Port: i_wr_en_n; Dir: Input; Width: 1; Type: LVL-REQ; Function: Write enable (macro WEB); Active: Active-low
Port: i_wr_addr; Dir: Input; Width: LPARA_ADDR_W; Type: LVL-DATA; Function: Write address (macro AW); Active: -
Port: i_wr_data; Dir: Input; Width: PARA_AFIFO_DATA_W; Type: LVL-DATA; Function: Write data (macro DW); Active: -
Port: i_clk_rd; Dir: Input; Width: 1; Type: CLK; Function: Read clock (macro CLKR); Active: Rising edge
Port: i_rd_en_n; Dir: Input; Width: 1; Type: LVL-REQ; Function: Read enable (macro REB). Tied to 0 by m_vlsit_afifo_mem; Active: Active-low
Port: i_rd_addr; Dir: Input; Width: LPARA_ADDR_W; Type: LVL-DATA; Function: Read address (macro AR); Active: -
Port: o_rd_data; Dir: Output; Width: PARA_AFIFO_DATA_W; Type: LVL-DATA; Function: Read data (macro QR), latency 1; Active: -
Generic SRAM macro and its model VLSIT_CELL_SRAM_1W1R (defined by the author, vendor-neutral, no datasheet needed).
Pins: CLKW, WEB, AW, DW, BWEB, CLKR, REB, AR, QR.
Write: at the rising edge of CLKW with WEB = 0, each bit of DW whose BWEB bit is 0 is written to the word at AW.
The wrapper ties BWEB to all zeros (whole-word write).
Read: at the rising edge of CLKR with REB = 0, QR shows the word at AR after the edge (read latency of 1 CLKR cycle).
QR keeps its value while REB = 1.
A read and a write of the same address at the same time: the model VLSIT_CELL_SRAM_1W1R (DEC-041) returns the old word and the stored word is not corrupted.
A real library macro may return an unknown value; the value is ignored because o_empty = 1 (Section 10.5).
The names are generic foundry-style names, not the pins of a specific vendor macro.
The real macro is mapped in the body of the wrapper. m_vlsit_afifo_ram_macro instantiates VLSIT_CELL_SRAM_1W1R as u_dont_touch_sram and nothing else, in every flow (DEC-043).

VLSIT_CELL_SRAM_1W1R is a synthesizable RTL model in 000_Common/rtl_cells (DEC-041): the array is inferred as a memory, the write port is in the CLKW domain with the bit mask BWEB, and QR is a register of the CLKR domain.
Its module, parameter, and pin names keep the style of a library macro and are exempt from the naming rule of REF-003.
There is no external protocol.
The write and read interfaces are enable-based:
Case: Write with space; Legal behavior: i_wr_en = 1 and full = 0: word stored; Illegal / unsupported case: -; IP response: Accept; Requirement IDs: REQ-FUNC-004
Case: Write while full; Legal behavior: i_wr_en = 1 and full = 1; Illegal / unsupported case: Overflow; IP response: Reject, raise overflow; Requirement IDs: REQ-ERR-001
Case: Read with data; Legal behavior: i_rd_en = 1 and empty = 0: pointer advances; Illegal / unsupported case: -; IP response: Accept; Requirement IDs: REQ-FUNC-005
Case: Read while empty; Legal behavior: i_rd_en = 1 and empty = 1; Illegal / unsupported case: Underflow; IP response: Reject, raise underflow; Requirement IDs: REQ-ERR-002
Case: Simultaneous write and read; Legal behavior: Allowed, different clock domains; Illegal / unsupported case: -; IP response: Independent; Requirement IDs: REQ-FUNC-001

Case: Software reset; Legal behavior: i_rst_n_sw = 0 (level, one cycle or more); Illegal / unsupported case: -; IP response: Four-phase handshake, both interfaces blocked, pointers reset (Section 10.7); Requirement IDs: REQ-SRST-001..018

Case: Write or read during the software reset; Legal behavior: i_wr_en or i_rd_en = 1; Illegal / unsupported case: Blocked access; IP response: Not accepted, no error pulse (DEC-028); Requirement IDs: REQ-SRST-003, REQ-SRST-008, REQ-SRST-017
Sampling edge: rising edge of the domain clock.
The input data stability requirement (hold of i_wr_data after the accepting edge) is none: the data is captured at the accepting edge.
No interrupt output.
Overflow and underflow are flags (Section 12).
If an interrupt is required, the integrator derives it from the flags.
Domain: CLK-WR; Clock port: i_clk_wr; Edge: Rising; Frequency range: No restriction; Source: SoC; Relationship to other clocks: Asynchronous to CLK-RD; Gating policy: None inside the IP
Domain: CLK-RD; Clock port: i_clk_rd; Edge: Rising; Frequency range: No restriction; Source: SoC; Relationship to other clocks: Asynchronous to CLK-WR; Gating policy: None inside the IP

Crossing ID: CDC-003; From → to: CLK-WR (storage) → CLK-RD; Signals: Stored data read by the read domain; Structure: No synchronizer. Data is stable by the pointer protocol (Section 10.4); Reset handling: None; Constraints / verification: EXC-003, SVA-004, CDC review

Crossing ID: CDC-004; From → to: Configuration source → CLK-WR / CLK-RD; Signals: i_full_thr, i_empty_thr, LPARA_PTR_W bits each; Structure: None. They are treated as asynchronous inputs without a synchronizer, because they are static: written once before the FIFO is used and not changed while it is in use (DEC-017); Reset handling: None; Constraints / verification: EXC-004; CDC waiver with this rationale

Crossing ID: CDC-005; From → to: CLK-WR → CLK-RD; Signals: Software reset request req_wr, 1 bit; Structure: Register in CLK-WR, then m_vlsit_afifo_sync (width 1, 2/3/4 stages) in m_vlsit_afifo_rd; Reset handling: Synchronizer reset by i_rst_n_rd, reset value 0; Constraints / verification: EXC-005, CDC lint

Crossing ID: CDC-006; From → to: CLK-RD → CLK-WR; Signals: Software reset acknowledge ack_rd, 1 bit; Structure: Register in CLK-RD, then m_vlsit_afifo_sync (width 1) in m_vlsit_afifo_wr; Reset handling: Synchronizer reset by i_rst_n_wr, reset value 0; Constraints / verification: EXC-006, CDC lint
Rules: no combinational logic between the launch Gray register and the first synchronizer stage, nor between stages (REF-003 P28).
Logic after the last stage (Gray to binary, compare) is allowed.
The bundled-data assumption of CDC-003 is documented here and shall be waived with this rationale in the CDC tool.
RDC: the software reset is a synchronous reset of the pointers and flags performed by the FSM of each domain; it adds no asynchronous reset and no reset-domain crossing.
The request and the acknowledge are level signals handled as CDC-005 and CDC-006.
The two hardware resets are independent inputs and need not be asserted together (DEC-009).
If only one domain is reset after the FIFO was used, the pointer state of the two domains becomes inconsistent.
The IP neither detects nor repairs this (ASM-005).

Reset ID: RST-WR; Port: i_rst_n_wr; Polarity / assertion: Active-low; Sync or async: Asynchronous assertion at the flops; already synchronized to i_clk_wr outside the IP; Scope: All write-domain state, the read-pointer synchronizer, flags; Deassertion: Controlled by the integrator, synchronous to i_clk_wr; Reset value: Pointers 0, full 0, overflow 0

Reset ID: RST-RD; Port: i_rst_n_rd; Polarity / assertion: Active-low; Sync or async: Asynchronous assertion at the flops; already synchronized to i_clk_rd outside the IP; Scope: All read-domain state, the write-pointer synchronizer, flags; Deassertion: Controlled by the integrator, synchronous to i_clk_rd; Reset value: Pointers 0, empty 1, underflow 0

Reset ID: RST-SW; Port: i_rst_n_sw; Polarity / assertion: Active-low level, write clock domain (DEC-025); Sync or async: Synchronous: acts through the FSMs of both domains, not through the asynchronous reset pins; Scope: Write pointer and write flags (write FSM), read pointer and read flags (read FSM). The storage is not cleared (DEC-035); Deassertion: After the handshake of Section 10.7, read side first; Reset value: Pointers 0, o_empty = 1, o_full = 0
Control and validity state (pointers, flags) are reset.

The FIFO storage is resetless; its content is not consumed until the write pointer proves it was written (REF-003 SEQ-04). o_rd_data while empty is the storage content at the read pointer, which is undefined until written.
Reset sequencing: the two resets are independent (ASM-005).
Stopped-clock behavior and warm/partial reset: the IP has no special handling.
Retention reset: not supported.
Hardware reset priority (DEC-031): i_rst_n_wr and i_rst_n_rd act asynchronously on the FSMs and pointers of their domain at any time, also during a software reset.
If only one domain gets a hardware reset during a software reset, the handshake can wait forever for the other domain; the IP does not repair it (ASM-005 applies).
DFT is N/A (DEC-003): the IP provides no test-mode control of the resets.
N/A: no power-intent requirement was given.
The IP contains no isolation, retention, or power-domain logic.
Parameters use parameter logic [31:0] PARA_AFIFO_ with the three comment lines required by REF-003 PAR-02.
Derived constants use localparam logic [31:0] LPARA_ placed in the parameter port list after the parameters.
The RTL has no elaboration check for illegal values (DEC-002 closed). $clog2 may be used for the derived widths (DEC-019 closed).

Parameter: PARA_AFIFO_DATA_W; Purpose: Data bit width; Default: 32; Legal values / range: Minimum 1, no upper limit; Dependencies / invalid combinations: None; Effect: Width of i_wr_data, o_rd_data, storage

Parameter: PARA_AFIFO_CELL_TYPE; Purpose: Synchronizer cell selection: 0 = bypass, 1 = two D flip-flop cells in series, 2 = one 2-FF cell, 3 = one 3-FF cell, 4 = one 4-FF cell. Present on the top, wr, rd, sync, and cell_sync; the same value for both crossings; Default: 2; Legal values / range: 0, 1, 2, 3, 4; Dependencies / invalid combinations: The cell sets S = 0, 2, 2, 3, 4 stages. Option 0 has no synchronization and shall not be used for the pointer crossings (Section 14.4); Effect: Latency of the flags (Section 10.3), MTBF, synchronizer cell

Parameter: PARA_AFIFO_CELL_RST_VAL (cell wrapper); Purpose: 0 = flop cell with asynchronous reset to 0, 1 = flop cell with asynchronous set to 1; Default: 0; Legal values / range: 0, 1; Dependencies / invalid combinations: One value per synchronizer bit, taken from PARA_AFIFO_SYNC_RST_VAL; Effect: Selects the reset or set flavour of the cell

Parameter: PARA_AFIFO_MEM_USE_MACRO; Purpose: 0 = RTL array, 1 = library SRAM wrapper; Default: 0; Legal values / range: 0, 1; Dependencies / invalid combinations: Uses the generic macro model of Section 6.2 until a real macro is mapped in the wrapper; Effect: Storage branch

Parameter: PARA_AFIFO_SYNC_W (sync module); Purpose: Number of synchronized bits; Default: None (set by the parent to LPARA_PTR_W); Legal values / range: 1 or more; Dependencies / invalid combinations: -; Effect: Width of the synchronizer

Parameter: PARA_AFIFO_SYNC_RST_VAL (sync module); Purpose: Reset value of every synchronizer stage; Default: 0; Legal values / range: Vector of PARA_AFIFO_SYNC_W bits, one reset value per bit (DEC-010); Dependencies / invalid combinations: The value shall be a legal Gray pointer value for the pointer crossings (0); Effect: Reset state of the stages
Parameter: LPARA_ADDR_W; Purpose: log2 of the depth; Default: Derived; Legal values / range: -; Dependencies / invalid combinations: PARA_AFIFO_DEPTH; Effect: Address width
Parameter: LPARA_PTR_W; Purpose: LPARA_ADDR_W + 1; Default: Derived; Legal values / range: -; Dependencies / invalid combinations: PARA_AFIFO_DEPTH; Effect: Pointer width

Illegal configurations are: depth not a power of 2, depth below 2, stage count outside 2..4, and option parameter outside 0..1.
The IP does not check them (DEC-002 closed) and its behavior with an illegal value is undefined.
Quantity: Binary pointer; Width: LPARA_PTR_W; Encoding / range: Unsigned, 0 .. 2 x depth - 1, wraps; Extension / truncation: None; Overflow / invalid behavior: Wraps by design
Quantity: Address; Width: LPARA_ADDR_W; Encoding / range: Low bits of the binary pointer, 0 .. depth - 1; Extension / truncation: Truncation of the MSB; Overflow / invalid behavior: None
Quantity: Gray pointer; Width: LPARA_PTR_W; Encoding / range: gray = bin XOR (bin >> 1); Extension / truncation: None; Overflow / invalid behavior: Changes one bit per increment

Quantity: Gray to binary (after the synchronizer); Width: LPARA_PTR_W; Encoding / range: Bit i of binary = XOR of Gray bits i..LPARA_PTR_W-1; Extension / truncation: None; Overflow / invalid behavior: An invalid Gray value cannot occur in the model with one-bit changes

Quantity: Occupancy estimate; Width: LPARA_PTR_W; Encoding / range: Binary pointer difference, modulo 2 x depth; Extension / truncation: Explicit width cast; Overflow / invalid behavior: Pessimistic: it can differ from the true occupancy only by the pointer updates still inside the synchronizer
Quantity: Data word; Width: PARA_AFIFO_DATA_W; Encoding / range: Unsigned logic vector, bit 0 = LSB, no interpretation; Extension / truncation: None; Overflow / invalid behavior: None
Quantity: Flags; Width: 1; Encoding / range: 1 = condition true; Extension / truncation: None; Overflow / invalid behavior: -
All hardware data are unsigned 4-state logic vectors (REF-003 TYP-01).
No signed arithmetic is used.
The FIFO has no mode register.
Its state is the pair of pointers.

Mode/state: Empty; Entry condition: Reset, or all words read; Behavior: o_empty = 1, reads rejected; Exit condition: A write seen by the read domain; Outputs / side effects: o_underflow on a read request
Mode/state: Partial; Entry condition: Between empty and full; Behavior: Reads and writes accepted; Exit condition: Last word read, or last free entry written; Outputs / side effects: -

Mode/state: Full; Entry condition: All entries used (write view); Behavior: o_full = 1, writes rejected; Exit condition: A read seen by the write domain; Outputs / side effects: o_overflow on a write request

Mode/state: Software reset; Entry condition: i_rst_n_sw = 0 with the write FSM in RUN; Behavior: Both interfaces blocked, o_empty = 1, pointers reset by the handshake (Section 10.7); Exit condition: Both reset FSMs back in RUN (read side first); Outputs / side effects: o_sw_rst_busy (DEC-026)

Operation ID: OP-001 Write; Inputs / preconditions: i_wr_en = 1, o_full = 0; Processing semantics: Store data, increment write pointer, register Gray; Result / completion: Word queued; Latency / ordering: 1 write-clock cycle to update the pointer; visible to the read domain per Section 10.3

Operation ID: OP-002 Read; Inputs / preconditions: i_rd_en = 1, o_empty = 0; Processing semantics: Increment read pointer, register Gray; o_rd_data then shows the next word; Result / completion: The word was already on o_rd_data (show-ahead); Latency / ordering: No extra read latency: the next word is already read through the next-pointer address

Operation ID: OP-003 Overflow; Inputs / preconditions: i_wr_en = 1, o_full = 1; Processing semantics: Reject; Result / completion: 1-cycle o_overflow pulse; Latency / ordering: Pulse in the cycle after the request

Operation ID: OP-004 Underflow; Inputs / preconditions: i_rd_en = 1, o_empty = 1; Processing semantics: Reject; Result / completion: 1-cycle o_underflow pulse; Latency / ordering: Pulse in the cycle after the request

Operation ID: OP-005 Software reset; Inputs / preconditions: i_rst_n_sw = 0, write FSM in RUN; Processing semantics: Four-phase handshake: block, reset read pointer, acknowledge, reset write pointer, release read side, release write side; Result / completion: FIFO empty, both pointers 0, flags normal; Latency / ordering: About two request-acknowledge round trips plus the flush; example in Section 10.7.4
Let S = the number of stages of the cell selected by PARA_AFIFO_CELL_TYPE (2 for the options 1 and 2, 3 for the option 3, 4 for the option 4).
Counting destination clock edges after a source pointer register changes (edge 1 is the first destination edge after the change):
Cycle / event: Source edge t0; Input condition: Accepted write (or read); State/action: Binary and Gray pointer registers update; Output condition: The new Gray value is launched
Cycle / event: Destination edge 1; Input condition: -; State/action: Synchronizer stage 1 captures it; Output condition: -

Cycle / event: Destination edge S; Input condition: -; State/action: Last synchronizer stage holds it; Output condition: The flag, a combinational function of the synchronized pointer, changes after this edge
So a flag in the destination domain reflects a source pointer update after destination edge S (flags are combinational from the synchronized pointer, DEC-016).
With the metastability model (REQ-VER-001) the flag changes after destination edge S, S+1, or S+2 (edge 1 is the first edge after the change).
The flags are pessimistic in between (REQ-FUNC-008, REQ-FUNC-009).
o_rd_data is the storage output register; the read module gives the next-pointer address, so after an accepted read at edge R it shows the next word after R.
No arbitration: one write source, one read sink.
Depth: PARA_AFIFO_DEPTH entries.
Simultaneous write and read are independent; each domain only sees the other through its synchronizer.

Pointer protocol that makes CDC-003 safe: (a) the write pointer Gray register is updated at the same edge as the storage write, so any value seen by the read domain after S edges refers to entries already written; (b) an entry is rewritten only after the write domain has seen the read pointer pass it.
Read margin (DEC-022): the storage output register captures the word in every read-clock edge.

After a write, the first read-clock edge may capture an unsettled word. o_empty falls no earlier than the second read-clock edge after the write when the synchronizer has the nominal number of stages (S >= 2 edges to cross).
At that edge the word is clean, provided the path from the storage to the output register is shorter than one read-clock period (EXC-003).
The minimum latency is S >= 2 edges, also for the model (DEC-012).
Sustained throughput and minimum depth for full-rate operation: N/A, no target is specified (DEC-016).
The round-trip pointer latency is about 2 x S destination cycles, so the depth needed for full throughput grows with S and with the clock ratio.

Storage ID: MEM-001; Kind: FIFO array; Depth × width: PARA_AFIFO_DEPTH × PARA_AFIFO_DATA_W; Ports: 1 write (CLK-WR), 1 read (read side); Read latency: 1 read-clock cycle (registered output, next-pointer address); Write mask: None (whole word); Reset/init: None (resetless); ECC/parity: None; Implementation: Inferred array (default)

Storage ID: MEM-002; Kind: Library SRAM; Depth × width: Same; Ports: 1 write, 1 read; Read latency: 1 read-clock cycle; Write mask: None (BWEB tied to 0); Reset/init: None; ECC/parity: None; Implementation: Macro behind m_vlsit_afifo_ram_macro
Collision: a word that is valid (empty = 0) is never read while it is written, by the pointer protocol (Section 10.4).

A read of an address that is being written can still happen while the FIFO is empty because the storage is read every cycle (DEC-022); the macro model VLSIT_CELL_SRAM_1W1R then returns the old word of that address (Section 6.2), and the value is not used because o_empty = 1.
A real macro that returns an unknown value there is also acceptable.
Initialization: the content is undefined until written.
Reads are accepted only after a write (empty = 0). o_rd_data may show an undefined value while the entry at the read pointer was never written.
Invalid addresses: not possible, the address is the low pointer bits.
The macro wrapper provides no DFT/BIST hook or bypass, because DFT is N/A (DEC-003).
It must still present the show-ahead behavior of REQ-FUNC-017; the storage read is synchronous with the next-pointer address (DEC-022).
This section is informative.
It shows the behavior required by Sections 5, 6, 10, and 12 in detailed waveforms.

The FIFO figures (10.6.2, 10.6.3, 10.6.5) are drawn from a simulation (Icarus Verilog) of the real RTL of this IP, m_vlsit_afifo_top with the files of rtl, 000_Common/rtl_lib, and 000_Common/rtl_cells, driven by the waveform testbench waveforms/proto/tb_fifo_wave.sv (not a verification testbench).
The metastability figures (10.6.4) come from the demo waveforms/proto/meta_demo.sv, which has the same model as the simulation branch of m_vlsit_afifo_cell_sync.
Every figure is an SVG file in waveforms/.
Reproduction steps are in Section 10.6.6.

Item: Synchronous interfaces; Value: Every input of the write interface (i_wr_en, i_wr_data) changes at a rising edge of i_clk_wr, and every input of the read interface (i_rd_en) at a rising edge of i_clk_rd: the testbench assigns them at the edge, so the design samples the new value at the next rising edge. The resets are asserted and released at a rising edge of their clock. The outputs change after a rising edge of their own clock (registers, pulses) or follow the registers combinationally (the flags). Each run is checked: the line "Check of the write/read interface inputs" under each event table counts the changes outside a rising edge, and it is 0

Item: Clocks of 10.6.2 and 10.6.3; Value: i_clk_wr period 10 ns (rising edges at 5 + 10 k ns). i_clk_rd period 14 ns (rising edges at 7 + 14 k ns). The edges coincide every 70 ns

Item: Configuration of 10.6.5; Value: PARA_AFIFO_DEPTH = 8, PARA_AFIFO_DATA_W = 8, S = 2, both clocks with a period of 10 ns, the read clock 3 ns later than the write clock (rising edges at 5 + 10 k ns and 8 + 10 k ns)
Item: Thresholds; Value: i_full_thr = 3 (6 in 10.6.5) and i_empty_thr = 1 (static)
Item: Colors; Value: Blue = write domain. Orange = read domain. Green = storage (RTL array or SRAM macro). Violet = model internals. A red bus = unknown value (X)
Item: Red-circled numbers; Value: Event numbers. Each number is explained in the event table next to the figure and drawn as a dashed line through all waveforms

Item: Signal types; Value: i_wr_en, i_rd_en: level requests (LVL-REQ). o_full, o_empty, o_full_thr, o_empty_thr: levels (LVL-STS). o_overflow, o_underflow: one-cycle pulses (PULSE). See the legend in Section 6.2

Item: Rows "write accept" and "read accept"; Value: The accept condition of the design: the request is 1, the side is not blocked, and the FIFO is not full (empty). It is a level during the cycle before the edge; the word is taken at the rising edge that ends the cycle

Stimulus of 10.6.2 and 10.6.3 (the values are driven at an edge and taken at the next one): words 0x11, 0x22, 0x33, 0x44 driven at write edges 95 to 125 and taken at 105 to 135 (the FIFO becomes full); a fifth word (0x55) driven at 135 and taken at 145 (overflow); i_rd_en driven at read edge 161, so that five reads are sampled at 175 to 231 (the fifth is an underflow); one word 0x66 driven at write edge 245 and taken at 255 while the FIFO is empty; one read of it driven at read edge 287 and taken at 301.

sentences.text: Figure 10.6-1: complete scenario.
Figure 10.6-2: zoom on the first write, the crossing of the write pointer, and the fall of o_empty.
Figure 10.6-3: zoom on a write to an empty FIFO whose read port reads the same entry in every cycle.
Event table of Figures 10.6-1 to 10.6-3:

No.: 1; Time (ns): 105.0; Event: Write of 0x11 accepted at write edge 105 (i_wr_en = 1 since edge 95, o_full = 0). The storage is written and the write Gray pointer register changes 000 -> 001 at the same edge.

No.: 2; Time (ns): 119.0; Event: o_rd_data shows 0x11 (show-ahead). The storage is read in every read cycle with the address of the next read pointer (0), so it already holds the new word before the empty flag falls.

No.: 3; Time (ns): 133.0; Event: The write Gray pointer has crossed the 2-stage synchronizer (S = 2 read edges after the first capturing edge) and o_empty falls (combinational from the synchronized pointer). The data was already on o_rd_data.
No.: 4; Time (ns): 135.0; Event: The 4th word (0x44) is accepted at write edge 135 and fills the FIFO: o_full rises.

No.: 5; Time (ns): 145.0; Event: A 5th write (0x55) is sampled at write edge 145 while o_full = 1: it is dropped (pointer and storage unchanged) and o_overflow pulses for one write cycle, then i_wr_en falls at the same edge.

No.: 6; Time (ns): 175.0; Event: First read accepted at read edge 175 (i_rd_en = 1 since edge 161, o_empty = 0). o_rd_data moves to the next word 0x22 right after this edge, because the read module gave the address of the next read pointer.
No.: 7; Time (ns): 195.0; Event: The read Gray pointer has crossed to the write domain (2 write edges) and o_full falls.
No.: 8; Time (ns): 217.0; Event: The 4th read (edge 217) takes the last word: o_empty rises.
No.: 9; Time (ns): 231.0; Event: A 5th read is sampled at read edge 231 while o_empty = 1: the read pointer is unchanged and o_underflow pulses for one read cycle. i_rd_en falls at the same edge.

No.: 10; Time (ns): 255.0; Event: Write to an empty FIFO: a new word (0x66) is written to address 0 at write edge 255. The read pointer addresses the same entry and the storage is read at every read edge, but no read edge happened since the write, so o_rd_data still shows the old word 0x11.
No.: 11; Time (ns): 259.0; Event: The next read edge (259) captures the new word: o_rd_data = 0x66. o_empty is still 1.
No.: 12; Time (ns): 273.0; Event: The new write pointer has crossed to the read domain: o_empty falls.
No.: 13; Time (ns): 301.0; Event: The word 0x66 is read at read edge 301 and o_empty rises again.
Check of the write interface inputs: 0 change(s) of i_wr_en, i_wr_data outside a rising edge of the clock Check of the read interface inputs: 0 change(s) of i_rd_en outside a rising edge of the clock
What the figures show:

Write path.
A write is accepted at the write edge where i_wr_en = 1 and o_full = 0.
The array and the write pointer both update at that edge (event 1).
Show-ahead read.
The read module gives the address of the next read pointer every cycle, so the storage output register already holds the next word. o_rd_data shows 0x11 before o_empty falls (events 2 and 3).
After an accepted read (event 6), o_rd_data moves to the next word without extra latency.
Pessimistic flags. o_empty falls S = 2 read edges after the first capturing edge of the write pointer (event 3). o_full falls late after the first read (event 7), not at the read edge.
Neither flag is ever early.
Pulses. o_overflow (event 5) and o_underflow (event 9) are registered, one cycle wide, and return to 0 by themselves.
The rejected request leaves the pointers and the storage unchanged.
Write to an empty FIFO (events 10 to 12).
The word is written at edge 255; the read register still shows the old word of address 0 until the next read edge (259, event 11), which captures 0x66; o_empty falls two read edges later (event 12).

sections.title: Metastability model of the synchronizer (simulation branch, REQ-VER-001)

sentences.text: The model is the branch of m_vlsit_afifo_cell_sync compiled when VLSIT_SYNTHESIS is not defined (Section 14.1, DEC-038); m_vlsit_afifo_sync and the other modules only instantiate the wrapper.
It models the extra delay caused by metastability.
Each bit of the synchronized vector is independent.
When a bit changes at the input of the last stage, the model chooses, from a seed, an extra delay of 0, 1, or 2 destination cycles.
With 0 extra cycles the output equals the plain chain.
If the input changes again while a change is pending, the pending value is replaced by the new input value and the delay restarts.
The model is controlled by +AFIFO_MSYNC_EN (enable) and +AFIFO_MSYNC_SEED (seed).
The figures use seed 1 and a source-domain period of 10 ns against a destination period of 14 ns.
Every input change is launched at a rising edge of the source clock.
The Gray pointer bits step through 000, 001, 011, 010, 110, 111, six source cycles apart.

Bit 3 is a fast-toggling bit that is added only to show the replacement of a pending change: it toggles once per source cycle (10 ns, shorter than the destination period of 14 ns); it is not part of a pointer.

No.: 2; Time (ns): 231.0; What happens: Bit 0 changes to 0 at the last synchronizer stage. The model chose 2 extra cycle(s): latency 3 cycles after the first capturing edge, so the model output changes 28 ns after the plain chain output.

No.: 3; Time (ns): 301.0; What happens: Bit 2 changes to 1 at the last synchronizer stage. The model chose 0 extra cycle(s): latency 1 cycles after the first capturing edge, so the model output changes 0 ns after the plain chain output.
No.: 4; Time (ns): 441.0; What happens: Bit 3: the pending change to 1 is replaced by the new input value 0; the delay restarts.

What the figures show:
The row "plain chain" is the model with the model disabled, the row "meta model" is the model with the delay chosen.
They are equal when the chosen extra delay is 0 and the meta model is later by 1 or 2 destination periods otherwise.
The rows "latency chosen" show the delay selected at each change of each bit.
Different bits of the same signal can get different delays.
A Gray pointer changes one bit per update, so a late bit makes the destination domain see the previous pointer value for a while instead of the new one.
A pending change that is replaced (event 4) can make a short pulse disappear on the model output.
This is intended: the model is there to check that the FIFO flags stay pessimistic when a bit arrives late (REQ-FUNC-008, REQ-FUNC-009).
The delay of the flags at the FIFO ports is therefore S, S + 1, or S + 2 destination edges after the first capturing edge (Section 10.3).
The FIFO of Section 10.6.2 uses the plain chain, which is the case of 0 extra cycles.
This scenario shows the FIFO working at the full rate of one word per clock cycle on both sides, without any interruption (no stall, no empty or full cycle).
The two clocks have the same period (10 ns), with the read clock 3 ns after the write clock, and the depth is 8.
The producer writes 24 words (0x01 to 0x18) in 24 consecutive write cycles.
The consumer sets i_rd_en = 1 at the first read edge after it has seen o_empty = 0, keeps it, and drops it at the edge of the 24th accepted read.
All inputs change at rising edges of their clock.

What the figures show:

No interruption on the write side. i_wr_en is 1 from the first to the last word, a word is accepted at every write edge (the check line gives 24 accepted edges and 0 gaps), and o_full stays 0 for the whole burst.
No interruption on the read side.

From the first accepted read (event 3) to the last (event 6) a word is accepted at every read edge (24 accepted edges, 0 gaps), o_empty stays 0 until the last word is read, and o_rd_data steps through the consecutive words 0x01, 0x02, 0x03, ... in the order of the writes.
Start-up delay only.
The first read is accepted about 33 ns after the first write: the word crosses the synchronizer (S = 2 read edges, event 2) and the consumer needs one more edge to set i_rd_en.

This delay is paid once; after it the two sides run at the same rate and the number of words in the FIFO stays at 4 (write pointer minus read pointer, counted at the read edges) until the writes stop.
Pointers.

Both Gray pointers change by one bit at every edge (INV-003), and the binary pointers wrap from 15 to 0 (pointer width 4 for depth 8) while the storage address wraps from 7 to 0, without any effect on the flow.
No error flag.
No overflow and no underflow pulse occurs during the burst.
Condition.
The rate is kept because the two clocks have the same frequency.
With a slower read clock the FIFO fills and o_full stops the producer (10.6.2); with a faster read clock o_empty stops the consumer.

The tool bin and lib directories of the suite shall both be on PATH.

Files in waveforms/proto: tb_fifo_wave.sv (waveform testbench of the RTL, scenarios 1 and 2, array and macro), meta_demo.sv (metastability model and demo), wavelib.py (VCD to SVG renderer), gen_all.py (figures, event tables, and the synchronism check), run_waveforms.py (driver).
The waveforms of the software reset are in Section 10.7.4.
The software reset returns the FIFO to the empty state without a hardware reset.
The input i_rst_n_sw is an active-low level that belongs to the write clock domain.
Because the two pointers live in two unrelated clock domains, the reset is a handshake between the domains and not a single signal.
Write side first blocks, then asks.
From the cycle in which i_rst_n_sw = 0, writes are blocked.
The write reset FSM raises the request req_wr, which crosses to the read domain (CDC-005).
Read side blocks, resets, answers.
When the synchronized request is 1, reads are blocked and o_empty = 1.
The read reset FSM resets the read pointer and raises the acknowledge ack_rd, which crosses to the write domain (CDC-006).
Write side resets its pointer after the answer.
The write pointer is reset only after the acknowledge is seen, so the write pointer is never reset before the read side has stopped using the old pointer.
The write FSM then holds until i_rst_n_sw = 1.
Four-phase release.
The write side drops the request, the read side drops the acknowledge, and each side leaves the reset only when its synchronized copy of the other pointer is 0 (flush check, 10.7.3).
The read side leaves first.
The write side leaves last, because its release needs the acknowledge to be 0, which is the effect of the read release.
What is lost.
The words in the FIFO are discarded.
A read accepted between the assertion of i_rst_n_sw and the arrival of the request in the read domain returns a valid pre-reset word; its word is discarded anyway.
The storage is not cleared (DEC-035).
Write reset FSM (CLK-WR) and read reset FSM (CLK-RD):
Block conditions (combinational, zero latency (DEC-030)):
Signal: wr_blk; Definition: (write FSM not in RUN) OR (i_rst_n_sw = 0), which is o_sw_rst_busy OR (i_rst_n_sw = 0)
Signal: rd_blk; Definition: (read FSM not in RUN) OR req_sync
Signal: Write accepted; Definition: i_wr_en AND NOT wr_blk AND NOT the normal full condition
Signal: Read accepted; Definition: i_rd_en AND NOT rd_blk AND NOT the normal empty condition
Signal: o_empty; Definition: rd_blk OR the normal empty condition
Signal: o_full; Definition: 1 while wr_blk (DEC-027); otherwise the normal full condition
Signal: o_full_thr, o_empty_thr; Definition: Values of an empty FIFO while wr_blk (write side) or rd_blk (read side) (DEC-029); otherwise normal
Signal: o_overflow, o_underflow; Definition: No pulse for an access blocked by the software reset (DEC-028)

Signal: o_sw_rst_busy; Definition: Flip-flop reg_sw_rst_busy: set when the write FSM leaves RUN, cleared when it returns to RUN; equal to (write FSM not in RUN) at every clock edge (DEC-026, Section 10.7.7)
The pointers are reset synchronously by the FSMs.
The FSM state registers are reset by the hardware resets (i_rst_n_wr, i_rst_n_rd).
Handshake sequence:

sections.title: Behavior per phase and the flush check

sentences.text: Phase: P0 Normal; Trigger: -; Write side: RUN, writes accepted; Read side: RUN, reads accepted; o_empty: Normal; o_full (DEC-027): Normal; req: 0; ack: 0; o_sw_rst_busy: 0

Phase: P1 Request; Trigger: i_rst_n_sw = 0; Write side: Writes blocked in the same cycle. Next write edge: REQ, req_wr = 1; Read side: Reads still accepted (request not seen); o_empty: Normal; o_full (DEC-027): 1; req: 0 to 1; ack: 0; o_sw_rst_busy: 0, then 1 at the next write edge (with req_wr)

Phase: P2 Request crosses; Trigger: S read edges; Write side: REQ, waits; Read side: When the synchronized request = 1: reads blocked in that cycle; o_empty: 1; o_full (DEC-027): 1; req: 1; ack: 0; o_sw_rst_busy: 1

Phase: P3 Read reset; Trigger: Read FSM sees the request; Write side: REQ; Read side: RST: read pointer = 0, then ACK with ack_rd = 1; o_empty: 1; o_full (DEC-027): 1; req: 1; ack: 0 to 1; o_sw_rst_busy: 1

Phase: P4 Ack crosses; Trigger: S write edges; Write side: Sees the acknowledge: PTR, write pointer = 0, then HOLD; Read side: ACK, waits; o_empty: 1; o_full (DEC-027): 1; req: 1; ack: 1; o_sw_rst_busy: 1
Phase: P5 Hold; Trigger: i_rst_n_sw stays 0; Write side: HOLD, writes blocked; Read side: ACK; o_empty: 1; o_full (DEC-027): 1; req: 1; ack: 1; o_sw_rst_busy: 1
Phase: P6 Release request; Trigger: i_rst_n_sw = 1; Write side: HOLD to REL, req_wr = 0; Read side: ACK; o_empty: 1; o_full (DEC-027): 1; req: 1 to 0; ack: 1; o_sw_rst_busy: 1

Phase: P7 Read release; Trigger: Synchronized request = 0 and synchronized write pointer = 0; Write side: REL, writes still blocked; Read side: ACK to RUN, ack_rd = 0. Flags live (empty = 1, both pointers 0); o_empty: Normal (1); o_full (DEC-027): 1; req: 0; ack: 1 to 0; o_sw_rst_busy: 1 (the read release does not change it)

Phase: P8 Write release; Trigger: Synchronized acknowledge = 0 and synchronized read pointer = 0; Write side: REL to RUN: writes unblocked, full live; Read side: RUN; o_empty: Normal; o_full (DEC-027): Normal (0); req: 0; ack: 0; o_sw_rst_busy: 1, then 0 at the release edge
Flush check.
After a pointer is reset, the other domain still holds a synchronized copy of the old value for a few cycles.
If the read side were released while its copy of the write pointer is still the old non-zero value, o_empty would fall and a word that never existed would be read.
The same holds for the write side and the full flag.
The release therefore needs the synchronized pointer of the other side to be 0.
The negative run of Section 10.7.6 (flush check removed) fails in 23 of 36 runs, so the check is necessary.

All waveforms come from the protocol prototype waveforms/proto/srst_proto.sv (3-bit pointers, depth 4, i_wr_en and i_rd_en driven by the testbench, write clock 10 ns, read clock 14 ns, S = 2 stages, plain synchronizers, thresholds i_full_thr = 3 and i_empty_thr = 1).

The prototype models the closed decisions DEC-025 to DEC-036: active-low i_rst_n_sw, o_sw_rst_busy, o_full = 1 while writes are blocked, no error pulse for a blocked access, threshold flags of an empty FIFO while blocked, zero-latency blocks, and hardware reset priority.
It is not the RTL of the IP.
Blue = write domain, orange = read domain, red-circled numbers = events of the tables.
Four scenarios are drawn:
Scenario: 1; What it shows: Main sequence with three words in the FIFO; the producer and the consumer keep requesting during the reset; Figures: 10.7-1 to 10.7-4
Scenario: 2; What it shows: Full FIFO with the producer in overflow, and a reset requested by a one-cycle low pulse of i_rst_n_sw; Figures: 10.7-5
Scenario: 3; What it shows: i_rst_n_sw asserted again while the write FSM is in REL: a new sequence follows; Figures: 10.7-6
Scenario: 4; What it shows: Hardware reset of both domains in the middle of the sequence: clean restart; Figures: 10.7-7
Synchronous interfaces.

In all scenarios every input of the write interface (i_wr_en, i_wr_data) and the software reset i_rst_n_sw change at a rising edge of i_clk_wr, every input of the read interface (i_rd_en) at a rising edge of i_clk_rd, and the hardware resets are asserted and released at a rising edge of their clock (the testbench assigns them at the edge, so the design samples the new value at the next edge).

Scenario: 4; Write domain signals checked (clock i_clk_wr): i_wr_en, i_wr_data, i_rst_n_sw, rst_n_wr; Changes outside a rising edge: 0; Read domain signals checked (clock i_clk_rd): i_rd_en, rst_n_rd; Changes outside a rising edge: 0
Scenario 1: main sequence.

What the figures show (scenario 1):

Write side, from event 1. i_wr_en stays 1 until event 13 and nothing is accepted: the write pointer does not move and the storage is not written. o_full = 1 in the cycle in which i_rst_n_sw falls (zero latency), o_full_thr takes the value of an empty FIFO (0), and o_overflow does not pulse. o_sw_rst_busy = 1 from event 2 to event 13.
Read side, from event 3.
Between events 1 and 3 the consumer still reads (read pointer 0 to 1 to 2): the request has not reached the read domain, and these reads return valid pre-reset words.
From event 3 reads are blocked: i_rd_en stays 1 and nothing is accepted, o_empty = 1 and o_empty_thr = 1.
Order.
The read pointer is reset (event 4) before the acknowledge rises (event 5); the write pointer is reset (event 7) only after the acknowledge is seen (event 6).
Release.

Event 11 (read released) is 25 ns before event 13 (write released): the order is forced by the handshake, because the write release needs the acknowledge to be 0, which is the effect of the read release.
After the read release (event 11) the consumer still requests a read; the FIFO is empty and the access is no longer blocked, so o_underflow pulses once.
This is the normal underflow of the FIFO, not an effect of the reset.
After event 13 the first write is accepted (event 14), and o_empty and o_empty_thr fall only after the write pointer has crossed to the read domain (event 15).
The read pointer then runs 0, 1, 2 for the two new words.
Scenario 2: one-cycle pulse on a full FIFO.
The FIFO is full (four words), the producer keeps writing, and i_rst_n_sw is low for exactly one write-clock cycle.

No.: 3; Time (ns): 166.0; Event: Write FSM takes the request at the first write edge: req_wr = 1, o_sw_rst_busy = 1.
No.: 4; Time (ns): 166.0; Event: i_rst_n_sw is back to 1 after one cycle. The request is already latched, so the sequence continues.
No.: 5; Time (ns): 191.0; Event: The request is visible in the read domain: reads blocked, o_empty = 1.
No.: 6; Time (ns): 219.0; Event: Read pointer reset, ack_rd = 1.
No.: 7; Time (ns): 246.0; Event: Write pointer reset (PTR). The input is already 1, so the FSM does not wait in HOLD.
No.: 8; Time (ns): 266.0; Event: Write FSM: req_wr = 0.
No.: 9; Time (ns): 303.0; Event: Read side released first.
No.: 10; Time (ns): 326.0; Event: Write side released last: o_full falls, writes unblocked.
No.: 11; Time (ns): 376.0; Event: The first write after the reset is accepted.
What the figure shows: the write FSM latches the request at the first write edge, so a one-cycle pulse is enough (event 3).

Before the pulse the producer is in overflow (o_overflow pulses, event 1); from the pulse on, the same i_wr_en = 1 causes no overflow pulse because the access is blocked. o_full stays 1 during the whole reset and falls at the write release (event 10); o_full_thr follows the empty-FIFO value while blocked.
Because the input is already 1, the write FSM passes HOLD without waiting.
Scenario 3: assertion again while the write FSM is in REL (DEC-032). i_rst_n_sw is released, and is driven to 0 again while the write FSM is in REL (before the write release).
The producer keeps i_wr_en = 1.
Figure 10.7-6: i_rst_n_sw asserted again in REL.
No.: 1; Time (ns): 196.0; Event: First software reset: i_rst_n_sw = 0, writes blocked, handshake starts.
No.: 2; Time (ns): 316.0; Event: i_rst_n_sw back to 1 (after HOLD): the write FSM goes to REL and drops the request.
No.: 3; Time (ns): 326.0; Event: Write FSM in REL, waiting for the acknowledge to fall.
No.: 4; Time (ns): 336.0; Event: i_rst_n_sw = 0 again while the write FSM is in REL. Writes stay blocked (the block includes the input); i_wr_en = 1 is not accepted.
No.: 5; Time (ns): 359.0; Event: First sequence: the read side is released.
No.: 6; Time (ns): 386.0; Event: First sequence: the write FSM reaches RUN. The input is still 0, so no write is accepted in this cycle either (wr_blk includes the input).
No.: 7; Time (ns): 396.0; Event: Second sequence starts at once: req_wr = 1.
No.: 8; Time (ns): 496.0; Event: i_rst_n_sw back to 1 (in HOLD of the second sequence).
No.: 9; Time (ns): 541.0; Event: Second sequence: the read side is released again after its own reset.
No.: 10; Time (ns): 566.0; Event: Second sequence: the write side is released last. Writes are unblocked.

What the figure shows: writes stay blocked all the time, also in the cycle in which the write FSM reaches RUN with the input still 0 (the block includes the input); no write is accepted between the two sequences.

The second sequence starts at once (event 7) and completes in the same way (read released first, event 9; write released last, event 10). o_sw_rst_busy falls for one write-clock cycle between the two sequences (the FSM is in RUN while the input is still asserted), while o_full stays 1 and writes stay blocked.
Scenario 4: hardware reset during the sequence (DEC-031).
Both hardware resets are asserted in the middle of the sequence, with the write reset released first and the read reset released later.
The testbench keeps the traffic idle until both domains are out of reset (ASM-005).
Figure 10.7-7: hardware reset of both domains during the sequence.
No.: 1; Time (ns): 206.0; Event: Software reset starts: i_rst_n_sw = 0.
No.: 2; Time (ns): 216.0; Event: req_wr = 1.
No.: 3; Time (ns): 261.0; Event: The read side is reset and ack_rd = 1.
No.: 4; Time (ns): 296.0; Event: The write pointer is reset; the write FSM waits in HOLD.

No.: 5; Time (ns): 326.0; Event: Hardware reset of both domains asserted (i_rst_n_wr = 0, i_rst_n_rd = 0) in the middle of the sequence; the testbench also releases i_rst_n_sw. Both FSMs, both pointers and both synchronizers go to their reset values at once (hardware reset priority).
No.: 6; Time (ns): 366.0; Event: i_rst_n_wr released. The write FSM is in RUN and the FIFO is empty.
No.: 7; Time (ns): 401.0; Event: i_rst_n_rd released (later than the write side). The read FSM is in RUN and o_empty = 1.
No.: 8; Time (ns): 496.0; Event: The first write after the reset is accepted (0xA5) once both domains are out of reset (ASM-005).
No.: 9; Time (ns): 527.0; Event: o_empty falls after the write pointer has crossed to the read domain.

What the figure shows: both FSMs, both pointers, and both request and acknowledge synchronizers return to their reset values at the assertion of the hardware resets (event 5), whatever the state of the handshake.
After the release the FIFO is empty (o_empty = 1, o_full = 0, pointers 0, FSMs in RUN) and works normally: a word is written (event 8), crosses (event 9), and is read.

ID: CC-01; Case: i_rst_n_sw is a one-cycle low pulse; Behavior: Captured by the write FSM at the first write edge where it is 0; the sequence completes (DEC-026); Evidence: Scenario 2; random widths 1 to 12 cycles

ID: CC-02; Case: i_rst_n_sw stays low for a long time; Behavior: The write FSM waits in HOLD and writes stay blocked; the read side is released while the write side still waits; Evidence: Scenario 1 (low for 13 write cycles); random

ID: CC-03; Case: i_rst_n_sw asserted again while the write FSM is in REL; Behavior: Writes stay blocked; a new sequence starts when the FSM is back in RUN. o_sw_rst_busy falls for one cycle between the two sequences (DEC-032); Evidence: Scenario 3; random mode 1

ID: CC-04; Case: Read between the assertion and the arrival of the request; Behavior: Accepted as a normal read of pre-reset data; the word is discarded by the reset; Evidence: Scenario 1, events 1 to 3
ID: CC-05; Case: Write in the same edge in which i_rst_n_sw falls; Behavior: Rejected: the block is combinational from the input (DEC-030); Evidence: Scenarios 1 to 3

ID: CC-06; Case: Read or write attempted during the reset; Behavior: Rejected without an error pulse (DEC-028). A read of the empty FIFO right after the read release gives a normal underflow pulse; Evidence: Scenarios 1, 2
ID: CC-07; Case: Storage content; Behavior: Not cleared; o_rd_data shows the word at address 0 while the FIFO is empty, as after a hardware reset (DEC-035); Evidence: By construction

ID: CC-08; Case: Hardware reset during the software reset; Behavior: Hardware reset has priority. A reset of both domains gives a clean restart. A reset of one domain only leaves the other domain waiting for the handshake and is not repaired (DEC-031, ASM-005); Evidence: Scenario 4; random mode 2
ID: CC-09; Case: A clock stops during the reset; Behavior: The handshake waits until the clock runs again (DEC-036); Evidence: By construction

ID: CC-10; Case: Random extra latency on every crossing; Behavior: The four-phase handshake is level based, so a longer delay only lengthens the sequence; the multi-bit pointers are protected by the flush check (DEC-034); Evidence: Regression, model on
ID: CC-11; Case: Threshold flags during the reset; Behavior: Values of an empty FIFO (o_full_thr = 0 for i_full_thr > 0, o_empty_thr = 1) (DEC-029); Evidence: Scenario 1
