sentences.text: Needs iverilog and vvp with both the bin and lib directories of the OSS CAD Suite on PATH.
Run: Scripted scenarios 1 to 4; Setting: The runs drawn in Section 10.7.4; Result: All pass (scenario 1: read released at 401 ns, write released at 426 ns)

Run: Positive, mode 0; Setting: Seeds 1 to 12, half-periods (write, read) in {(5,7), (3,11), (11,3)} ns, metastability model off and on, 20 random software resets per run, random traffic, scoreboard; the next reset starts after the write release; Result: 72 of 72 pass
Run: Positive, mode 1; Setting: Same, with i_rst_n_sw asserted again at any time (also in REL); Result: 72 of 72 pass
Run: Positive, mode 2; Setting: Same as mode 1, and a quarter of the resets are aborted by a hardware reset of both domains; Result: 72 of 72 pass
Run: Negative; Setting: Mode 1, model on, flush check removed (+NOFLUSH=1); Result: 13 of 36 pass, 23 of 36 fail (a side is released with a stale synchronized pointer)

Checks of the prototype: o_sw_rst_busy (a flip-flop) equals "write FSM not in RUN" at every write-clock edge; no write accepted while wr_blk; no read accepted while rd_blk; o_full = 1 and o_full_thr = value of an empty FIFO while the write side is blocked; o_empty = 1 and o_empty_thr = 1 while the read side is blocked; no read of a word that was never written; data of every accepted read equals the written word (scoreboard); at each release the own pointer and the synchronized pointer of the other side are 0; the read release is before the write release and after the request; empty = 1 while both pointers are 0 after the read release; after a hardware reset both FSMs are in RUN, both pointers are 0, o_empty = 1, and o_full = 0; a deadlock timeout.
Not covered by this evidence (added with the RTL): formal proof of SVA-007 to SVA-016; a hardware reset of one domain only; stopped clocks.
o_sw_rst_busy is the status of the write side of the software reset.
It is driven directly by the flip-flop reg_sw_rst_busy (REQ-SRST-018), so it changes only at a rising edge of i_clk_wr and never glitches.
It follows the write reset FSM:

Write FSM state: RUN; What happens in the state: Normal operation. If i_rst_n_sw = 0 is seen, the FSM leaves RUN; o_sw_rst_busy: 0; How the state is entered (edge of i_clk_wr): After reset, or at the edge where REL ends (flop cleared at this edge)

Write FSM state: REQ; What happens in the state: req_wr = 1, waiting for the synchronized acknowledge; o_sw_rst_busy: 1; How the state is entered (edge of i_clk_wr): At the edge where the FSM sees i_rst_n_sw = 0 in RUN (flop set at this edge, together with req_wr)
Write FSM state: PTR; What happens in the state: Write pointer reset (one cycle); o_sw_rst_busy: 1; How the state is entered (edge of i_clk_wr): At the edge where the synchronized acknowledge is seen
Write FSM state: HOLD; What happens in the state: Waits for i_rst_n_sw = 1; o_sw_rst_busy: 1; How the state is entered (edge of i_clk_wr): After PTR

Write FSM state: REL; What happens in the state: req_wr = 0, waits for the acknowledge = 0 and the synchronized read pointer = 0 (flush check); o_sw_rst_busy: 1; How the state is entered (edge of i_clk_wr): At the edge where i_rst_n_sw = 1 is seen in HOLD

Write FSM state: RUN (again); What happens in the state: Write side released; o_sw_rst_busy: 0; How the state is entered (edge of i_clk_wr): At the edge where the release condition holds (flop cleared at this edge)
Timing rules (all from the simulations of Section 10.7.4):

Rule: R1; Statement: The write block wr_blk follows i_rst_n_sw in the same cycle (combinational). o_sw_rst_busy rises at the first write-clock edge after i_rst_n_sw falls, so it is up to one write-clock cycle behind the block.; Measured (scenario 1): i_rst_n_sw falls at 226 ns, wr_blk and o_full rise at 226 ns, busy rises at 236 ns
Rule: R2; Statement: o_sw_rst_busy rises at the same edge as req_wr.; Measured (scenario 1): Both at 236 ns

Rule: R3; Statement: o_sw_rst_busy does not follow i_rst_n_sw after it has risen: it stays 1 when the input returns to 1 (HOLD, REL).; Measured (scenario 1): The input rises at 356 ns, busy stays 1 until 426 ns

Rule: R4; Statement: o_sw_rst_busy does not follow the read FSM. The read side is released first, and busy falls only when the write side is released.; Measured (scenario 1): Read released at 401 ns, busy falls at 426 ns (25 ns later)
Rule: R5; Statement: o_sw_rst_busy falls at the same edge where the write FSM returns to RUN, together with wr_blk and o_full (when i_rst_n_sw = 1).; Measured (scenario 1): All three fall at 426 ns

Rule: R6; Statement: wr_blk = o_sw_rst_busy OR (i_rst_n_sw = 0) at every cycle.; Measured (scenario 1): By construction; every prototype run checks that busy equals "write FSM not in RUN" (SVA-015, SVA-016)
Rule: R7; Statement: A hardware reset of the write domain clears o_sw_rst_busy asynchronously, at any state of the sequence.; Measured (scenario 1): Scenario 4: falls at 326 ns with i_rst_n_wr

Rule: R8; Statement: If i_rst_n_sw = 0 is seen again in REL, busy falls for exactly one write-clock cycle between the two sequences (the FSM is in RUN for one cycle), and writes stay blocked during the gap because i_rst_n_sw = 0.; Measured (scenario 1): Scenario 3: busy low from 386 ns to 396 ns
Figure 10.7-8: o_sw_rst_busy against the write FSM state, the block, and the read side (scenario 1).
No.: 1; Time (ns): 226.0; Event: i_rst_n_sw falls. wr_blk = 1 and o_full = 1 at once (combinational). o_sw_rst_busy is still 0: it is a flip-flop and changes only at the next write-clock edge.

No.: 2; Time (ns): 236.0; Event: The first write-clock edge after the fall: the write FSM goes RUN to REQ, and req_wr and o_sw_rst_busy rise at this same edge (busy is one write-clock cycle behind the block).
No.: 3; Time (ns): 316.0; Event: The acknowledge was seen, the write FSM goes REQ to PTR and resets the write pointer. Busy stays 1 (state not RUN).
No.: 4; Time (ns): 356.0; Event: i_rst_n_sw back to 1. The write FSM is in HOLD and goes to REL at the next edge. Busy stays 1: it follows the FSM state, not the input.
No.: 5; Time (ns): 401.0; Event: The read FSM returns to RUN (read side released). Busy stays 1: it describes the write side, which is released last.
No.: 6; Time (ns): 426.0; Event: The write FSM returns to RUN. o_sw_rst_busy falls at this edge, together with wr_blk and o_full: writes are possible again.
Figure 10.7-9: o_sw_rst_busy in the one-cycle gap between two sequences (scenario 3).
No.: 1; Time (ns): 336.0; Event: i_rst_n_sw = 0 again while the write FSM is in REL (first sequence not finished). Busy is still 1.
No.: 2; Time (ns): 386.0; Event: The write FSM returns to RUN: o_sw_rst_busy falls. wr_blk stays 1 because the input is still 0.
No.: 3; Time (ns): 396.0; Event: One write-clock cycle later the FSM sees the input at 0 in RUN and goes to REQ: o_sw_rst_busy rises again. Writes were blocked during the whole gap.
Measured intervals of o_sw_rst_busy and of the write block in the four scenarios:
Scenario: 1; i_rst_n_sw falls (ns): 226.0; wr_blk rises (ns): 226.0; o_sw_rst_busy rises (ns): 236.0; o_sw_rst_busy falls (ns): 426.0; wr_blk falls (ns): 426.0; Busy high (write-clock cycles): 19
Scenario: 2; i_rst_n_sw falls (ns): 156.0; wr_blk rises (ns): 156.0; o_sw_rst_busy rises (ns): 166.0; o_sw_rst_busy falls (ns): 326.0; wr_blk falls (ns): 326.0; Busy high (write-clock cycles): 16
Scenario: 3.1; i_rst_n_sw falls (ns): 196.0; wr_blk rises (ns): 196.0; o_sw_rst_busy rises (ns): 206.0; o_sw_rst_busy falls (ns): 386.0; wr_blk falls (ns): 566.0; Busy high (write-clock cycles): 18
Scenario: 3.2; i_rst_n_sw falls (ns): 336.0; wr_blk rises (ns): 196.0; o_sw_rst_busy rises (ns): 396.0; o_sw_rst_busy falls (ns): 566.0; wr_blk falls (ns): 566.0; Busy high (write-clock cycles): 17
Scenario: 4; i_rst_n_sw falls (ns): 206.0; wr_blk rises (ns): 206.0; o_sw_rst_busy rises (ns): 216.0; o_sw_rst_busy falls (ns): 326.0; wr_blk falls (ns): 326.0; Busy high (write-clock cycles): 11

Notes on the table: in scenario 3 the write block is continuous from 197 ns to 566 ns while busy has two intervals (rows 3.1 and 3.2) separated by the one-cycle gap; in scenario 4 busy falls when the hardware reset is applied (event 5 of that scenario), not at a write release.
The time from the rise of the block to the rise of busy is less than one write-clock period (the input changes shortly after the previous edge in these runs).
What software and the integrator may conclude:
Observation: o_sw_rst_busy = 1; Meaning: A software reset is in progress on the write side. Writes are blocked. The read side may already be released

Observation: o_sw_rst_busy = 0 and i_rst_n_sw = 1; Meaning: The reset is complete or none is running: both sides are released (the read side was released before the write side) and the FIFO is empty if it was reset

Observation: o_sw_rst_busy = 0 and i_rst_n_sw = 0; Meaning: The request has been asserted and not yet taken (at most one write-clock cycle), or the one-cycle gap between two sequences (R8). Writes are blocked by the input
Observation: Rise of o_sw_rst_busy; Meaning: The request was taken by the write FSM and will be answered by the read side
Observation: Fall of o_sw_rst_busy; Meaning: End of the sequence: writes are accepted again from this cycle
o_sw_rst_busy belongs to the write clock domain.
The IP has no synchronizer for it: a consumer in the read domain that needs it shall synchronize it itself, or use o_empty, which is 1 during the whole reset of the read side.
N/A (DEC-003 closed).
This IP has no software-visible register and no CSR workbook (REF-005 is not used).
Overflow and underflow are 1-cycle pulses, so there is no sticky status register.
The software reset input i_rst_n_sw is driven by a control register outside the IP.
Item: CSR workbook file; Specification: N/A
Item: Sheet used for this IP; Specification: N/A
Item: Workbook revision / date; Specification: N/A

Software reset sequence for the owner of the control register of i_rst_n_sw: (1) stop the producer if it should not lose words; (2) drive i_rst_n_sw to 0 (one write-clock cycle is enough; it may be held longer); (3) drive i_rst_n_sw back to 1 after the reset has started.

The FIFO is usable again, on both sides, when o_sw_rst_busy = 0 and i_rst_n_sw = 1 (DEC-026, Section 10.7.7): the read side is always released before the write side, and o_sw_rst_busy falls when the write side is released.

Do not use o_sw_rst_busy = 0 alone while i_rst_n_sw is held at 0: for one write-clock cycle after the fall of i_rst_n_sw, and in the one-cycle gap between two sequences (Section 10.7.5), the output is 0 while writes are blocked.
The words in the FIFO at the reset are lost.

Error ID: ERR-001; Detection condition: i_wr_en = 1 while full (write domain); Observable response/status: o_overflow 1-cycle pulse (registered, in the cycle after the rejected request). The write is dropped: storage and write pointer unchanged; Interrupt: None; Clear/recovery: Self-clearing after one cycle; Reset behavior: Cleared by i_rst_n_wr

Error ID: ERR-002; Detection condition: i_rd_en = 1 while empty (read domain); Observable response/status: o_underflow 1-cycle pulse (registered, in the cycle after the rejected request). The read pointer is unchanged. o_rd_data still shows the word at the read pointer; Interrupt: None; Clear/recovery: Self-clearing after one cycle; Reset behavior: Cleared by i_rst_n_rd

Error ID: ERR-003; Detection condition: Reset asserted in one domain only, after the FIFO was used; Observable response/status: FIFO state inconsistent; not detected; Interrupt: None; Clear/recovery: Reset both domains; Reset behavior: Integrator responsibility (ASM-005)

Error ID: ERR-004; Detection condition: Illegal parameter; Observable response/status: Not detected by the IP (DEC-002); behavior undefined; Interrupt: None; Clear/recovery: Fix the configuration; Reset behavior: N/A

Error ID: ERR-005; Detection condition: i_wr_en or i_rd_en = 1 while blocked by a software reset; Observable response/status: The access is not accepted. No o_overflow or o_underflow pulse (DEC-028); Interrupt: None; Clear/recovery: Ends with the software reset release; Reset behavior: Not applicable

Error ID: ERR-006; Detection condition: i_rst_n_sw = 0 while a software reset is already in progress; Observable response/status: Ignored until the write FSM is back in RUN; a new sequence then starts if it is still 0 (DEC-032); Interrupt: None; Clear/recovery: Automatic; Reset behavior: Cleared by the hardware resets
Precedence: the two error flags belong to different domains and do not interact.
A simultaneous write and read on the same cycle cannot produce both errors for the same event.
No retry or drain is provided; the producer or consumer shall react to the flags.

Do not claim timing closure from RTL synthesis alone.
The SDC and analysis flow for clocks, I/O delays, uncertainty, exceptions, and corners are linked in Section 17.
REF-003 is the mandatory RTL authority.

At minimum: one module per .sv file, the file name equals the module name, the top is a structural wrapper, ANSI ports with input wire and output logic, unsigned 4-state logic, parameters parameter logic [31:0] PARA_AFIFO_ with the PAR-02 comments, always_comb and always_ff only, named connections, no tab characters, branch statements on their own line (FIL-04), module ports aligned in columns (FIL-05) and declared in functional groups (FIL-06), comment lines at most 100 characters, and the file header of REF-003 FIL-01.
Project-specific consequences:
Synchronizer flip-flops and the technology cells exist only in m_vlsit_afifo_cell_sync; m_vlsit_afifo_sync contains only instances of it (CLK-02, HIE-07, DEC-039).
The memory macro exists only in m_vlsit_afifo_ram_macro.
The metastability model is the branch of m_vlsit_afifo_cell_sync that is compiled when the macro VLSIT_SYNTHESIS is not defined; no other module contains it (DEC-038).
It is a simulation model: it is written in professional SystemVerilog and is not bound by the RTL rules of REF-003 (DEC-001, DEC-021).
The synthesis, lint, CDC, formal, and equivalence flows shall define VLSIT_SYNTHESIS (REQ-RTL-002); REF-003 P12 allows referencing a macro that is defined by the flow.

The same macro selects the branches of m_vlsit_afifo_cell_sync only: with the macro it instantiates the library cells (the synthesizable stand-in models VLSIT_CELL_SYNC_* of 000_Common/rtl_cells are used until the real library views exist); without it it contains the behavioral simulation model with the metastability model. m_vlsit_afifo_ram_macro has no branch and always instantiates VLSIT_CELL_SRAM_1W1R.
The flag, the Gray register, and the pointer registers are one-process-per-state elements with separate next-state logic.
The software reset FSMs are one-process-per-state elements with separate next-state logic; the state registers follow the FSM naming of REF-003, for example reg_fsm_srst_current_state.
They live in m_vlsit_afifo_wr and m_vlsit_afifo_rd because the top has no logic (REQ-FUNC-011).

The request and acknowledge synchronizers are instances of m_vlsit_afifo_sync with PARA_AFIFO_SYNC_W = 1. o_sw_rst_busy is the output of its own flip-flop reg_sw_rst_busy (REQ-SRST-018), not a decode of the FSM state.
Names: every name defined in the m_vlsit_afifo_* modules uses the abbreviations of REF-003 NAM-08 and stays at 30 characters or less (NAM-07).

The number of synchronizer stages S is the stages of the selected cell: options 1 and 2: 2; option 3: 3; option 4: 4.

The latencies of Section 10.3 and the read margin of Section 10.4 hold for the options 1 to 4.

Option 0 has no synchronization: the Gray pointers would cross the domains without a synchronizer and the flag would change in the same cycle as the pointer, which breaks the read margin of Section 10.4 (at least 2 destination edges).
It is therefore not a legal option for the pointer crossings of this IP; it exists for a flow that inserts the synchronizer outside the IP.

ID: DEC-001; Decision: The metastability model is a simulation model. It is written in professional SystemVerilog, is not bound by the RTL rules, and is never used for synthesis.; Source: Requester; Effect: REQ-VER-001, Section 14.1

ID: DEC-002; Decision: (a) No elaboration check in the RTL. The legal parameter values are documented; the behavior with an illegal value is undefined.; Source: Requester; Effect: REQ-PARAM-003, ERR-004
ID: DEC-003; Decision: CSR is N/A. DFT is N/A (no port, no hook).; Source: Requester; Effect: Sections 6, 11, 16

ID: DEC-004; Decision: Defaults: 2 synchronizer stages, depth 8, data width 32. Depth has no upper limit but is a power of 2 (2^n). Data width has no upper limit (confirmed by the requester); minimum 1.; Source: Requester; Effect: Section 8
ID: DEC-005; Decision: Show-ahead read: o_rd_data is always the word at the current read pointer, including while empty. No o_rd_valid.; Source: Requester; Effect: REQ-FUNC-017

ID: DEC-006; Decision: Two separate threshold inputs. o_full_thr = occupancy >= i_full_thr. o_empty_thr = occupancy <= i_empty_thr. Both thresholds are static (control register, written once before use). All values are accepted; no legal-range restriction.; Source: Requester; Effect: REQ-FUNC-010, Section 6.2

ID: DEC-007; Decision: Overflow and underflow are registered 1-cycle pulses (DEC-020). An underflow read does not change the read pointer, and o_rd_data keeps showing the word at the read pointer.; Source: Requester; Effect: Section 12
ID: DEC-008; Decision: No fill-level output.; Source: Requester; Effect: Section 6

ID: DEC-009; Decision: Each domain has its own asynchronous-assert, active-low reset, synchronized to its clock outside the IP. The two resets need not be asserted at the same time. The clock frequencies and their ratio are unrestricted.; Source: Requester; Effect: Section 7, ASM-005
ID: DEC-010; Decision: Each synchronizer bit has its own reset value (vector).; Source: Requester; Effect: Section 8

ID: DEC-011; Decision: No library cell exists. The author creates example cell models, two flavours (asynchronous reset to 0, asynchronous set to 1), pins as in Section 14.4. The cell options are extended by DEC-037.; Source: Requester; Effect: Section 14.4, REQ-VER-003

ID: DEC-012; Decision: The model randomizes the latency of each bit independently. The latency is counted in cycles after the first capturing edge, nominal S-1, with 0, 1, or 2 extra cycles, i.e. S-1, S, S+1 (S = 2: 1, 2, 3; S = 3: 2, 3, 4; S = 4: 3, 4, 5); in edges from the input change the output changes at edge S, S+1, or S+2. If the input changes again during the delay, the new value replaces the pending change and the delay restarts. The model is controlled by plusargs (seed, enable); the plusarg names are the author's choice.; Source: Requester ("as proposed"); Effect: REQ-VER-001, Section 10.4

ID: DEC-013; Decision: The SRAM wrapper and model implement a generic foundry-style one-write-port, one-read-port interface defined by the author (Section 6.2). No vendor datasheet is required.; Source: Requester; Effect: m_vlsit_afifo_ram_macro, REQ-VER-002

ID: DEC-014; Decision: The FIFO array is a separate module, modelled as an SRAM with one write port and one read port so that it can be replaced by an ASIC SRAM macro, and it is instantiated in the top. The top therefore instantiates the write module, the read module, and the array module (this replaces the earlier wording that the top calls only two modules and that the array is called in the write module).; Source: Requester; Effect: REQ-FUNC-011, REQ-FUNC-015, REQ-CLK-004, Section 5

ID: DEC-015; Decision: document_id = VLSIT-AFIFO-SPEC; verification is a self-checking SystemVerilog testbench without UVM (author's choice as delegated). Technology, libraries, frequency, area, power, MTBF, and synthesis frontend are N/A (not specified).; Source: Requester ("N/A"); Effect: Header, Sections 13, 14, 15, 17

ID: DEC-016; Decision: The full, empty, and threshold flags are combinational from the synchronized pointers. Throughput and minimum-depth targets are N/A.; Source: Requester; Effect: REQ-FUNC-018, Section 10.3
ID: DEC-019; Decision: $clog2 may be used in the RTL for the derived widths.; Source: Requester; Effect: Section 8

ID: DEC-017; Decision: Timing bounds. EXC-001: set_max_delay of 0.9 x the period of the write clock for the write pointer. EXC-002: 0.9 x the period of the read clock for the read pointer. EXC-003: set_max_delay of 1 x the period of the receiving (read) clock for the data path between the write and read domains. The static threshold inputs are treated as asynchronous inputs without a synchronizer and excluded from timing by a false path (EXC-004, CDC-004). No set_min_delay is required.; Source: Requester; Effect: Section 17.1.3

ID: DEC-018; Decision: The timing exception of the read data path is set_max_delay of 1 x the period of the receiving (read) clock (EXC-003); decided together with DEC-017.; Source: Requester; Effect: Section 17.1.3
ID: DEC-020; Decision: The overflow and underflow pulses are registered and appear in the cycle after the rejected request.; Source: Requester; Effect: Sections 6.2, 12

ID: DEC-021; Decision: The macro VLSIT_SYNTHESIS (standard spelling) selects the branches of m_vlsit_afifo_sync, m_vlsit_afifo_cell_sync, and m_vlsit_afifo_ram_macro. The branch with the macro is the synthesizable model; the branch without it is the simulation model. A simulation defines the macro to run the synthesizable branch. The synthesis and analysis flows define it.; Source: Requester; Effect: REQ-VER-001, REQ-VER-002, REQ-VER-003, REQ-RTL-002, Section 14.1
ID: DEC-024; Decision: The macro name is VLSIT_SYNTHESIS. Its scope is m_vlsit_afifo_sync, m_vlsit_afifo_cell_sync, and m_vlsit_afifo_ram_macro.; Source: Requester; Effect: REQ-RTL-002

ID: DEC-022; Decision: (a) Both branches use a synchronous storage read. The read module drives the address of the next read pointer, the storage is read every read-clock cycle, and o_rd_data is the storage output. The RTL array has a read register clocked by i_clk_rd. There is no memory read enable.; Source: Requester; Effect: REQ-FUNC-017, Section 6.2, MEM-001, MEM-002

ID: DEC-023; Decision: The set_max_delay bound relative to the source clock is correct and preserves the Gray property. Consecutive pointer transitions are at least one source period apart and each path is bounded below one source period, so a transition completes before the next begins and the destination sees only valid Gray values at any frequency. No further skew constraint is needed. (The author's earlier concern about the destination period is withdrawn.); Source: Requester; Effect: EXC-001, EXC-002

ID: DEC-025; Decision: The software reset input is i_rst_n_sw, an active-low level (0 = reset requested), synchronous to the write clock i_clk_wr. Idle value 1. It is a control input sampled at the clock, not an asynchronous reset. (The author had proposed active-high i_sw_rst; the requester chose active-low and the name i_sw_reset_n. The naming rules fix the final spelling: NAM-08 abbreviates "reset" to "rst", and the naming table requires an active-low reset input to be i_rst_n_, so the input is i_rst_n_sw ("sw" = software reset source, in the write clock domain) and the busy output is o_sw_rst_busy.); Source: Requester; Effect: REQ-SRST-001, Sections 6.2, 7.3, 10.7

ID: DEC-026; Decision: i_rst_n_sw may be low for one write-clock cycle or for any longer time (level semantics; the FSM latches the request and waits in HOLD while it is low). The output o_sw_rst_busy exists and is driven directly by a flip-flop (no combinational logic on the output path).; Source: Requester ("as proposed"); Effect: REQ-SRST-001, REQ-SRST-013, Sections 6.2, 11.2

ID: DEC-027; Decision: o_full = 1 while the write side is blocked by the software reset; it returns to the normal full logic at the write release.; Source: Requester ("as proposed"); Effect: REQ-SRST-017, Section 10.7.2
ID: DEC-028; Decision: A write or read blocked by the software reset raises no o_overflow or o_underflow pulse.; Source: Requester ("as proposed"); Effect: REQ-SRST-017, ERR-005
ID: DEC-029; Decision: While blocked, o_full_thr and o_empty_thr take the values of an empty FIFO.; Source: Requester ("as proposed"); Effect: REQ-SRST-017

ID: DEC-030; Decision: The write block is combinational (zero latency) from i_rst_n_sw and the FSM state. It adds a combinational path from i_rst_n_sw to the write accept and the memory write enable.; Source: Requester ("as proposed"); Effect: REQ-SRST-008, Section 17.1.2

ID: DEC-031; Decision: The hardware resets have priority over the software reset. A hardware reset of one domain only during the sequence is not repaired (ASM-005 unchanged).; Source: Requester ("as proposed"); Effect: REQ-SRST-015, Section 7.3

ID: DEC-032; Decision: i_rst_n_sw asserted again while the write FSM is in REL: writes stay blocked and a new sequence starts when the FSM is back in RUN.; Source: Requester ("as proposed"); Effect: REQ-SRST-016, ERR-006

ID: DEC-033; Decision: The request and acknowledge crossings use set_max_delay of 0.9 x the source clock period, like the pointers (EXC-005, EXC-006).; Source: Requester ("as proposed"); Effect: Section 17.1.3
ID: DEC-034; Decision: The flush check is kept: a side is released only when the synchronized pointer of the other side is 0.; Source: Requester ("as proposed"); Effect: REQ-SRST-010, Section 10.7.3
ID: DEC-035; Decision: The software reset does not clear the storage; only the pointers and flags are reset.; Source: Requester ("as proposed"); Effect: REQ-SRST-014
ID: DEC-036; Decision: Both clocks run during the whole software reset; there is no timeout (ASM-006).; Source: Requester ("as proposed"); Effect: ASM-006, CC-09

ID: DEC-037; Decision: The cell wrapper selects its cell by PARA_AFIFO_CELL_TYPE: 0 bypass, 1 two D-FF cells in series, 2 one 2-FF cell, 3 one 3-FF cell, 4 one 4-FF cell; the simulation branch has one model per option with the same function. The cell names are the author's choice on the requester's delegation: VLSIT_CELL_SYNC_DFF_*, VLSIT_CELL_SYNC_2FF_*, VLSIT_CELL_SYNC_3FF_*, VLSIT_CELL_SYNC_4FF_*. The author also chose, and the requester accepted by decision DEC-039: one wrapper per bit in the synchronizer; default option 2; option 0 is not legal for the pointer crossings; a value above 4 gives the 4-FF cell.; Source: Requester, author's choice; Effect: REQ-FUNC-014, REQ-VER-003, Sections 8, 14.4

ID: DEC-038; Decision: The metastability model lives only in the simulation branch of m_vlsit_afifo_cell_sync (one bit, options 1 to 4 of PARA_AFIFO_CELL_TYPE), with the semantics of DEC-012 and the plusargs of REQ-VER-001. m_vlsit_afifo_sync has no model of its own: it only instantiates m_vlsit_afifo_cell_sync for every bit (DEC-039), and the other modules only instantiate m_vlsit_afifo_sync. The instance names of cells and macros follow u_dont_touch_ (REQ-RTL-003).; Source: Requester; Effect: REQ-VER-001, REQ-RTL-003, Sections 10.6.4, 14.1, 14.4

ID: DEC-039; Decision: m_vlsit_afifo_sync only instantiates m_vlsit_afifo_cell_sync, one per bit. The pure RTL flip-flop chain is removed, and so are the parameters PARA_AFIFO_SYNC_USE_CELL and PARA_AFIFO_SYNC_STAGE: the number of stages S is set by the cell option PARA_AFIFO_CELL_TYPE (0, 2, 2, 3, 4). m_vlsit_afifo_wr, m_vlsit_afifo_rd, and m_vlsit_afifo_top keep only PARA_AFIFO_CELL_TYPE (default 2). The macro VLSIT_SYNTHESIS no longer selects anything in m_vlsit_afifo_sync. The default configuration therefore uses the example cell models until real library cells exist.; Source: Requester; Effect: REQ-FUNC-013, REQ-FUNC-014, Sections 8, 14.1, 14.4

ID: DEC-040; Decision: The example technology cell models are synthesizable RTL under the RTL rules, one module per file in the folder 000_Common/rtl_cells (VLSIT_CELL_SYNC_DFF_RN/SN, VLSIT_CELL_SYNC_2FF_RN/SN, VLSIT_CELL_SYNC_3FF_RN/SN, VLSIT_CELL_SYNC_4FF_RN/SN). Their pins follow the naming rule instead of a library pin style: i_clk_dst, i_rst_n_dst (RN) or i_set_n_dst (SN), i_d, o_q; the wrapper maps the pins of the real cell when it replaces them. The SRAM model VLSIT_CELL_SRAM_1W1R stays simulation-only.; Source: Requester; Effect: REQ-VER-003, Section 14.4

ID: DEC-041; Decision: The SRAM macro model VLSIT_CELL_SRAM_1W1R is synthesizable RTL (one module, file 000_Common/rtl_cells/VLSIT_CELL_SRAM_1W1R.sv, parameters ADDR_W and DATA_W, bit write mask BWEB, read data register QR, no reset). Its module name, parameter names, and pin names CLKW, WEB, AW, DW, BWEB, CLKR, REB, AR, QR keep the library-macro style and are exempt from the naming rule; all other rules apply. A read of the address written at the same edge returns the old word; the simulation branch of the wrapper still returns X there.; Source: Requester; Effect: REQ-VER-002, Section 6.2

ID: DEC-042; Decision: The example cell models of DEC-040 (VLSIT_CELL_SYNC_*) keep the usual pin names of a library cell, CK, RN or SN, D, Q, and are exempt from the naming rule for module and pin names, like the SRAM macro model (DEC-041); all other rules apply. This replaces the pin names i_clk_dst, i_rst_n_dst, i_set_n_dst, i_d, o_q of DEC-040.; Source: Requester; Effect: REQ-VER-003, Section 14.4

ID: DEC-043; Decision: m_vlsit_afifo_ram_macro only instantiates VLSIT_CELL_SRAM_1W1R. Its simulation branch (behavioral model returning X on a read-write collision) is removed, so the macro model of DEC-041 is used in simulation and in synthesis, and a read of an address written at the same edge returns the old word. The macro VLSIT_SYNTHESIS selects branches only in m_vlsit_afifo_cell_sync.; Source: Requester; Effect: REQ-VER-002, REQ-RTL-002, Sections 6.2, 10.5, 14.1

ID: DEC-044; Decision: The wrapper modules m_vlsit_afifo_cell_sync and m_vlsit_afifo_ram_macro are in the folder rtl_lib, separate from the FIFO logic in rtl; the example cells and the macro model stay in 000_Common/rtl_cells. Each folder has its own filelist.f.; Source: Requester; Effect: Section 14.2

ID: DEC-045; Decision: The port lists of all RTL modules are aligned in four columns (direction, type, width, name) and declared in functional groups with a comment per group, clock and reset first (REF-003 FIL-05, FIL-06; skill rules R-030, R-031). The earlier grouping by direction (HIE-03) is replaced. The groups of the top are write clock and reset, write interface, software reset, read clock and reset, read interface.; Source: Requester; Effect: Section 14.1, Section 6.2

ID: DEC-046; Decision: The folders rtl_lib and rtl_cells are moved to common_rtl/000_Common. Library wrappers, cells, and macro models of this and of every later IP are written in 000_Common, not in the folder of the IP. This replaces the location in DEC-044; the content and the roles are unchanged.; Source: Requester; Effect: Section 14.2

ID: DEC-047; Decision: The cell and macro models follow the skill rule R-032: the module name is VLSIT_CELL_, and the header states that the model is synthesizable RTL and that a real design uses the cell of the synthesis library. The models of this IP are renamed EX_SYNC_* to VLSIT_CELL_SYNC_* and EX_SRAM_1W1R to VLSIT_CELL_SRAM_1W1R; pin and parameter names keep the library style (DEC-041, DEC-042). Where an earlier decision names a model by its old name, the new name applies. The basic cells (gates, multiplexers, flip-flops, latches, clock cells) are delivered in the same folder 000_Common/rtl_cells.; Source: Requester; Effect: REQ-VER-003, Section 14.4
None.

Term / acronym: AFIFO; Definition: Asynchronous FIFO
Term / acronym: CDC; Definition: Clock-domain crossing
Term / acronym: RDC; Definition: Reset-domain crossing
Term / acronym: Gray code; Definition: Binary code in which consecutive values differ by one bit
Term / acronym: Binary pointer; Definition: Counter of LPARA_PTR_W bits; the extra MSB distinguishes full from empty
Term / acronym: Synchronizer; Definition: Chain of flip-flops that reduces the probability of metastability
Term / acronym: Metastability model; Definition: Simulation-only model that delays a synchronized change by a random number of cycles
Term / acronym: Overflow / underflow; Definition: A write to a full FIFO / a read from an empty FIFO
Term / acronym: Threshold flag; Definition: Flag raised before the FIFO is completely full or empty (definition in REQ-FUNC-010)
Term / acronym: SRAM macro; Definition: Library memory block, here with one write port and one read port
Term / acronym: Pessimistic flag; Definition: Flag that can be late to deassert but never early
Term / acronym: Software reset; Definition: Reset of both pointers and flags by a handshake between the two clock domains, started by i_rst_n_sw (Section 10.7)
Term / acronym: Flush check; Definition: Release condition of the software reset: the synchronized pointer of the other side is 0, so no stale pointer value is used after the release

The IP shall implement an asynchronous FIFO with an independent write clock domain and read clock domain.
The pointers shall cross between the two domains as Gray codes only. Each Gray pointer register shall change at most one bit per clock cycle of its own domain.
Words shall be read in the order they were written. Every accepted write shall be read exactly once. No word shall be lost, duplicated, or reordered.
A write shall be accepted at a write-clock edge when i_wr_en = 1 and the full flag is 0. It shall store i_wr_data in the entry addressed by the write pointer and advance the write pointer by one.
A read shall be accepted at a read-clock edge when i_rd_en = 1 and the empty flag is 0. It shall advance the read pointer by one. The read data interface is show-ahead (REQ-FUNC-017).

Each domain shall hold a binary pointer of LPARA_PTR_W = log2(depth) + 1 bits and a Gray pointer register derived from the next binary pointer. The Gray pointer register is the launch register of the crossing (no logic between it and the synchronizer).
The depth shall be a power of 2, because a Gray pointer wraps with a one-bit change only for a power-of-2 range. Minimum depth is 2. There is no upper limit on the depth (DEC-004).

The full flag is generated in the write domain. It shall be 1 whenever the write domain has no free entry, judged from the synchronized read pointer. It shall never be 0 while the FIFO is physically full. It may stay 1 late after a read frees an entry (pessimistic).

The empty flag is generated in the read domain. It shall be 1 whenever the read domain has no word to read, judged from the synchronized write pointer. It shall never be 0 while the FIFO is physically empty. It may stay 1 late after a write (pessimistic).

The IP shall provide o_full_thr (write domain) and o_empty_thr (read domain), each with its own threshold input. o_full_thr shall be 1 when the write-domain occupancy estimate is greater than or equal to i_full_thr. o_empty_thr shall be 1 when the read-domain occupancy estimate is less than or equal to i_empty_thr. The occupancy estimate is the binary write pointer minus the binary read pointer, where the pointer of the other domain is the synchronized one (Section 9); it is pessimistic for the full side (it can be larger than the true occupancy) and for the empty side (it can be smaller). Both flags are combinational. The thresholds are static: they are written once before the FIFO is used and do not change while it is in use. Every value of LPARA_PTR_W bits is accepted; the comparisons are defined for all of them (for example i_full_thr = 0 makes o_full_thr always 1, and a value above the depth makes it never 1).
m_vlsit_afifo_top shall be a structural wrapper that instantiates only m_vlsit_afifo_wr, m_vlsit_afifo_rd, and m_vlsit_afifo_mem.

m_vlsit_afifo_wr shall contain the write pointer logic, the full and threshold logic, the overflow logic, the synchronizer of the read Gray pointer, the write-side software reset FSM and the synchronizer of the acknowledge, and the memory write port outputs. m_vlsit_afifo_rd shall contain the read pointer logic, the empty and threshold logic, the underflow logic, and the synchronizer of the write Gray pointer, the read-side software reset FSM and the synchronizer of the request, and the memory read address output.

m_vlsit_afifo_sync shall provide a synchronizer with a configurable bit width and a reset value for every bit. The number of stages is set by PARA_AFIFO_CELL_TYPE: 2 stages for the options 1 and 2, 3 for the option 3, 4 for the option 4 (S in Section 10.3), and 0 for the option 0 (bypass, DEC-039).

m_vlsit_afifo_sync shall contain no flip-flop, cell, or model of its own: it shall instantiate only the wrapper m_vlsit_afifo_cell_sync, one wrapper per synchronized bit, in every configuration and in both branches of the macro VLSIT_SYNTHESIS (DEC-039). The wrapper shall select the cell by the parameter PARA_AFIFO_CELL_TYPE (DEC-037): 0 = bypass (o_q = i_d, no cell, no stage); 1 = two D flip-flop cells in series (2 stages); 2 = one 2-FF synchronizer cell (2 stages); 3 = one 3-FF synchronizer cell (3 stages); 4 = one 4-FF synchronizer cell (4 stages). Option 0 has no synchronization: it is not a legal choice for a Gray pointer crossing (Section 14.4).

m_vlsit_afifo_mem shall be an independent module instantiated in m_vlsit_afifo_top. It shall be modelled as an SRAM with one write port (write clock domain) and one read port (read clock domain), so that it can be replaced by an ASIC library SRAM macro.

m_vlsit_afifo_mem shall provide a generate branch that replaces the pure RTL array with a library SRAM that has one write port and one read port, through the wrapper m_vlsit_afifo_ram_macro. The default is the pure RTL array.

o_rd_data shall always show the word stored at the current read pointer, including while the FIFO is empty (show-ahead). It is the output of the synchronous storage read port: the read module drives the address of the next read pointer (the current read pointer, plus one if a read is accepted in this cycle) and the storage is read in every read-clock cycle, so after each read-clock edge o_rd_data is the word at the new read pointer. While empty or before the entry was ever written, its value is the storage content, which is undefined. There is no o_rd_valid; validity is o_empty = 0.
The full, empty, full-with-threshold, and empty-with-threshold flags shall be combinational functions of the local pointer registers and the synchronized pointer of the other domain.
The ports of every module shall be as listed in Section 6. The top ports do not depend on the parameter values.
The write and read clocks shall be treated as fully asynchronous. The IP shall not assume a phase or frequency relation. There is no restriction on the frequency or on the frequency ratio (DEC-009).

Every clock-domain crossing shall use a Gray pointer registered in its own domain, followed directly by m_vlsit_afifo_sync in the destination domain, with no logic before the first stage or between stages.
The read data path from the FIFO array (write-domain storage) to the read domain shall be valid whenever the pointer protocol of Section 10.4 allows a read.

m_vlsit_afifo_wr shall contain only logic of the write clock domain, and m_vlsit_afifo_rd shall contain only logic of the read clock domain. The FIFO array is a dual-clock storage owned by neither half; it is instantiated in the top (DEC-014).
i_rst_n_wr shall be already synchronized to i_clk_wr and i_rst_n_rd already synchronized to i_clk_rd. The IP shall not contain a reset synchronizer.

After reset (hardware reset, or the release of a software reset, REQ-SRST-012) the FIFO shall be empty: both pointers 0, full = 0, empty = 1, overflow = 0, underflow = 0. The flops use an asynchronous-assert, active-low reset. The two resets are independent and need not be asserted at the same time (ASM-005).
The number of entries (depth) shall be configurable by PARA_AFIFO_DEPTH.
The data bit width shall be configurable by PARA_AFIFO_DATA_W.

The legal parameter values are those of Section 8. The RTL shall not contain an elaboration check for illegal values (DEC-002); the behavior with an illegal value is undefined, and the verification configurations shall use legal values only.
When a write is requested while the FIFO is full, the overflow flag shall be raised and the write shall not change the stored data or the write pointer. The flag is a 1-cycle pulse (Section 12).

When a read is requested while the FIFO is empty, the underflow flag shall be raised and the read shall not change the read pointer. The flag is a 1-cycle pulse (Section 12); o_rd_data keeps showing the word at the current read pointer.

The IP shall have the input i_rst_n_sw, an active-low level in the write clock domain (DEC-025). A software reset sequence starts when i_rst_n_sw = 0 is seen at a write-clock edge while the write reset FSM is in RUN. The input may be held for one write-clock cycle or for any longer time (DEC-026).

The request shall be a register req_wr in m_vlsit_afifo_wr. It shall cross to the read domain through m_vlsit_afifo_sync (width 1, the same stage count as the pointers, CDC-005), with no logic before the first stage.
While the synchronized request is 1, or the read reset FSM is not in RUN, a read request shall not be accepted. The block is combinational (zero latency) from these two conditions.
From the cycle in which the read side is blocked until the read side is released, o_empty shall be 1.
When the read reset FSM has seen the request, it shall reset the read pointer (binary and Gray) to 0, and only then raise the acknowledge ack_rd (register in m_vlsit_afifo_rd).
The acknowledge shall cross to the write domain through m_vlsit_afifo_sync (width 1, same stage count, CDC-006), with no logic before the first stage.
When the write reset FSM has seen the synchronized acknowledge, it shall reset the write pointer (binary and Gray) to 0.

From the write-clock cycle in which i_rst_n_sw = 0, and until the write reset FSM is back in RUN, a write request shall not be accepted. The block is combinational (zero latency) from i_rst_n_sw and the FSM state (DEC-030).

The handshake shall have four phases: request up, acknowledge up, request down, acknowledge down. The request shall fall only after i_rst_n_sw = 1 and after the write pointer is reset. The acknowledge shall fall only after the request is seen at 0 in the read domain.

The read reset FSM shall leave its acknowledge state (return to RUN) only when the synchronized request is 0 and the synchronized write Gray pointer is 0. The write reset FSM shall return to RUN only when the synchronized acknowledge is 0 and the synchronized read Gray pointer is 0 (flush check, Section 10.7.3) (DEC-034).
After the software reset, the read side shall be released before the write side: the read FSM returns to RUN before the write FSM returns to RUN.
After the release, the flags shall be generated by the normal FIFO logic from the pointers. Both pointers are 0, so o_empty = 1 and o_full = 0 until the first write has crossed to the read domain.

The sequence shall complete for any width of i_rst_n_sw (one cycle or more), for any frequency and ratio of the two clocks, and with the metastability model enabled (random extra latency on every crossing).

The words that are in the FIFO when the software reset starts are discarded. A read accepted before the request reaches the read domain returns a valid pre-reset word. The storage content is not cleared (DEC-035).
A hardware reset of a domain shall have priority over the software reset: it resets the FSM and the pointers of its domain asynchronously (DEC-031).
If i_rst_n_sw = 0 is seen again while the write FSM is in REL, writes shall stay blocked and a new sequence shall start when the FSM is back in RUN (DEC-032).

During the software reset: o_full shall be 1 while the write side is blocked (DEC-027); a blocked write or read shall not raise o_overflow or o_underflow (DEC-028); o_full_thr and o_empty_thr shall take the values of an empty FIFO (DEC-029).

The output o_sw_rst_busy shall be the output of a dedicated flip-flop reg_sw_rst_busy of m_vlsit_afifo_wr, with no combinational logic between the flop and the port. It shall be set at the write-clock edge where the write reset FSM leaves RUN (the first edge at which the FSM takes the request) and cleared at the write-clock edge where it returns to RUN. It shall therefore be 1 in the states REQ, PTR, HOLD, and REL and 0 in RUN, at every write-clock edge, independently of the level of i_rst_n_sw and of the state of the read reset FSM. It shall be 0 after the hardware reset i_rst_n_wr (asynchronous clear). The write block is wr_blk = o_sw_rst_busy OR (i_rst_n_sw = 0).
The RTL shall comply with REF-003. Technology cells and memory macros shall appear only in the dedicated wrappers m_vlsit_afifo_cell_sync and m_vlsit_afifo_ram_macro.

The synthesis, lint, CDC, formal, and equivalence flows shall define the macro VLSIT_SYNTHESIS. In the branch selected by this macro, m_vlsit_afifo_cell_sync contains only instances of the library cells and follows REF-003. The branch of this module without the macro is simulation-only and is excluded from REF-003 (DEC-001, DEC-021). m_vlsit_afifo_sync and m_vlsit_afifo_ram_macro have a single branch and follow REF-003 in every flow (DEC-039, DEC-043). A simulation that defines VLSIT_SYNTHESIS runs the synthesizable branches.

The instance of every technology library cell and memory macro shall be named u_dont_touch_ (rule R-028, REF-003 NAM-09): u_dont_touch_dff_0, u_dont_touch_dff_1, u_dont_touch_sync2ff, u_dont_touch_sync3ff, u_dont_touch_sync4ff, u_dont_touch_sram. Instances of design modules keep u_.

m_vlsit_afifo_cell_sync shall contain a simulation model of the metastability of the synchronizer in the branch that is compiled when the macro VLSIT_SYNTHESIS is not defined (DEC-021, DEC-038). The wrapper is one bit, so every bit of a synchronizer is modelled independently; the model applies to the options 1 to 4 of PARA_AFIFO_CELL_TYPE (N = 2, 2, 3, 4 stages, the number S below is N), and the option 0 (bypass) has no stage and no model. No other module models metastability: m_vlsit_afifo_sync only instantiates m_vlsit_afifo_cell_sync for every bit, and the other modules only instantiate m_vlsit_afifo_sync (DEC-039). For every bit, when the input changes value, the model shall apply a random latency, chosen independently for each bit and each change. The latency is counted in destination clock cycles after the first capturing edge: the nominal value of an S-stage synchronizer is S-1 and the model adds 0, 1, or 2 extra cycles, so the latency is S-1, S, or S+1 (1, 2, 3 for S = 2; 2, 3, 4 for S = 3; 3, 4, 5 for S = 4). Counted in edges from the input change, with the first edge after the change as edge 1, the output changes at edge S, S+1, or S+2. If the input changes again during the delay, the new value replaces the pending change and the delay restarts. The model is written in professional SystemVerilog, is not bound by the RTL rules of REF-003, and is never used for synthesis (DEC-001). It is controlled by plusargs: +AFIFO_MSYNC_SEED= sets the random seed and +AFIFO_MSYNC_EN= enables the random latency, with 0 selecting the nominal latency. Without a plusarg the model is enabled with seed 1. The model prints its seed at the start of the simulation.

m_vlsit_afifo_ram_macro shall instantiate only the macro VLSIT_CELL_SRAM_1W1R, in every flow and in both branches of VLSIT_SYNTHESIS, with inputs and outputs matching the generic foundry-style interface of Section 6.2; it contains no simulation model of its own (DEC-043). VLSIT_CELL_SRAM_1W1R is the synthesizable RTL model of DEC-041 and stands in until a real library macro is mapped in the body of the wrapper.

Example technology cell models shall be delivered as synthesizable RTL, one module per file, in the folder 000_Common/rtl_cells, as stand-ins for the library cells, so that the synthesis branch of the cell wrapper can be simulated and synthesized with VLSIT_SYNTHESIS defined: VLSIT_CELL_SYNC_DFF_RN, VLSIT_CELL_SYNC_DFF_SN (one flop), VLSIT_CELL_SYNC_2FF_RN, VLSIT_CELL_SYNC_2FF_SN, VLSIT_CELL_SYNC_3FF_RN, VLSIT_CELL_SYNC_3FF_SN, VLSIT_CELL_SYNC_4FF_RN, VLSIT_CELL_SYNC_4FF_SN (a 2-, 3- or 4-flop synchronizer in one cell); the suffix RN means asynchronous active-low reset to 0 and SN asynchronous active-low set to 1. Each model shall follow REF-003 except the names: the module and pin names keep the usual style of a library cell, CK, RN (RN cells) or SN (SN cells), D, Q (DEC-040, DEC-042). In the branch without the macro, m_vlsit_afifo_cell_sync contains one behavioral model per PARA_AFIFO_CELL_TYPE option with the same function and the same number of stages as the cells of the synthesis branch, including the metastability model of REQ-VER-001 for the options 1 to 4. The models shall be replaced by the real library cells when available (DEC-011, DEC-037).

o_rd_data while empty shows the storage content at the read pointer; the consumer ignores it when o_empty = 1.

No FIFO operation (write or read) starts before both domains have left reset. Consequence, not a requirement: if one domain is reset alone after the FIFO was used, the pointer state of the two domains becomes inconsistent and the IP does not detect it.
Both clocks run during the whole software reset. If a clock stops, the handshake waits until it runs again; there is no timeout.
The metastability model is a simulation model. It is written in professional SystemVerilog, is not bound by the RTL rules, and is never used for synthesis.

Defaults: 2 synchronizer stages, depth 8, data width 32. Depth has no upper limit but is a power of 2 (2^n). Data width has no upper limit (confirmed by the requester); minimum 1.
Show-ahead read: o_rd_data is always the word at the current read pointer, including while empty. No o_rd_valid.

Two separate threshold inputs. o_full_thr = occupancy >= i_full_thr. o_empty_thr = occupancy <= i_empty_thr. Both thresholds are static (control register, written once before use). All values are accepted; no legal-range restriction.
Overflow and underflow are registered 1-cycle pulses (DEC-020). An underflow read does not change the read pointer, and o_rd_data keeps showing the word at the read pointer.

Each domain has its own asynchronous-assert, active-low reset, synchronized to its clock outside the IP. The two resets need not be asserted at the same time. The clock frequencies and their ratio are unrestricted.
Each synchronizer bit has its own reset value (vector).
No library cell exists. The author creates example cell models, two flavours (asynchronous reset to 0, asynchronous set to 1), pins as in Section 14.4. The cell options are extended by DEC-037.

The model randomizes the latency of each bit independently. The latency is counted in cycles after the first capturing edge, nominal S-1, with 0, 1, or 2 extra cycles, i.e. S-1, S, S+1 (S = 2: 1, 2, 3; S = 3: 2, 3, 4; S = 4: 3, 4, 5); in edges from the input change the output changes at edge S, S+1, or S+2. If the input changes again during the delay, the new value replaces the pending change and the delay restarts. The model is controlled by plusargs (seed, enable); the plusarg names are the author's choice.
The SRAM wrapper and model implement a generic foundry-style one-write-port, one-read-port interface defined by the author (Section 6.2). No vendor datasheet is required.

The FIFO array is a separate module, modelled as an SRAM with one write port and one read port so that it can be replaced by an ASIC SRAM macro, and it is instantiated in the top. The top therefore instantiates the write module, the read module, and the array module (this replaces the earlier wording that the top calls only two modules and that the array is called in the write module).

EXC-003: set_max_delay of 1 x the period of the receiving (read) clock for the data path between the write and read domains. The static threshold inputs are treated as asynchronous inputs without a synchronizer and excluded from timing by a false path (EXC-004, CDC-004). No set_min_delay is required.
The timing exception of the read data path is set_max_delay of 1 x the period of the receiving (read) clock (EXC-003); decided together with DEC-017.
The overflow and underflow pulses are registered and appear in the cycle after the rejected request.

The macro VLSIT_SYNTHESIS (standard spelling) selects the branches of m_vlsit_afifo_sync, m_vlsit_afifo_cell_sync, and m_vlsit_afifo_ram_macro. The branch with the macro is the synthesizable model; the branch without it is the simulation model. A simulation defines the macro to run the synthesizable branch. The synthesis and analysis flows define it.
The macro name is VLSIT_SYNTHESIS. Its scope is m_vlsit_afifo_sync, m_vlsit_afifo_cell_sync, and m_vlsit_afifo_ram_macro.

(a) Both branches use a synchronous storage read. The read module drives the address of the next read pointer, the storage is read every read-clock cycle, and o_rd_data is the storage output. The RTL array has a read register clocked by i_clk_rd. There is no memory read enable.

The set_max_delay bound relative to the source clock is correct and preserves the Gray property. Consecutive pointer transitions are at least one source period apart and each path is bounded below one source period, so a transition completes before the next begins and the destination sees only valid Gray values at any frequency. No further skew constraint is needed. (The author's earlier concern about the destination period is withdrawn.)

The software reset input is i_rst_n_sw, an active-low level (0 = reset requested), synchronous to the write clock i_clk_wr. Idle value 1. It is a control input sampled at the clock, not an asynchronous reset. (The author had proposed active-high i_sw_rst; the requester chose active-low and the name i_sw_reset_n. The naming rules fix the final spelling: NAM-08 abbreviates "reset" to "rst", and the naming table requires an active-low reset input to be i_rst_n_, so the input is i_rst_n_sw ("sw" = software reset source, in the write clock domain) and the busy output is o_sw_rst_busy.)

i_rst_n_sw may be low for one write-clock cycle or for any longer time (level semantics; the FSM latches the request and waits in HOLD while it is low). The output o_sw_rst_busy exists and is driven directly by a flip-flop (no combinational logic on the output path).
o_full = 1 while the write side is blocked by the software reset; it returns to the normal full logic at the write release.
A write or read blocked by the software reset raises no o_overflow or o_underflow pulse.
While blocked, o_full_thr and o_empty_thr take the values of an empty FIFO.
The write block is combinational (zero latency) from i_rst_n_sw and the FSM state. It adds a combinational path from i_rst_n_sw to the write accept and the memory write enable.
The hardware resets have priority over the software reset. A hardware reset of one domain only during the sequence is not repaired (ASM-005 unchanged).
i_rst_n_sw asserted again while the write FSM is in REL: writes stay blocked and a new sequence starts when the FSM is back in RUN.
The request and acknowledge crossings use set_max_delay of 0.9 x the source clock period, like the pointers (EXC-005, EXC-006).
The flush check is kept: a side is released only when the synchronized pointer of the other side is 0.
The software reset does not clear the storage; only the pointers and flags are reset.
Both clocks run during the whole software reset; there is no timeout (ASM-006).

The cell wrapper selects its cell by PARA_AFIFO_CELL_TYPE: 0 bypass, 1 two D-FF cells in series, 2 one 2-FF cell, 3 one 3-FF cell, 4 one 4-FF cell; the simulation branch has one model per option with the same function. The cell names are the author's choice on the requester's delegation: VLSIT_CELL_SYNC_DFF_*, VLSIT_CELL_SYNC_2FF_*, VLSIT_CELL_SYNC_3FF_*, VLSIT_CELL_SYNC_4FF_*. The author also chose, and the requester accepted by decision DEC-039: one wrapper per bit in the synchronizer; default option 2; option 0 is not legal for the pointer crossings; a value above 4 gives the 4-FF cell.

The metastability model lives only in the simulation branch of m_vlsit_afifo_cell_sync (one bit, options 1 to 4 of PARA_AFIFO_CELL_TYPE), with the semantics of DEC-012 and the plusargs of REQ-VER-001. m_vlsit_afifo_sync has no model of its own: it only instantiates m_vlsit_afifo_cell_sync for every bit (DEC-039), and the other modules only instantiate m_vlsit_afifo_sync. The instance names of cells and macros follow u_dont_touch_ (REQ-RTL-003).

m_vlsit_afifo_sync only instantiates m_vlsit_afifo_cell_sync, one per bit. The pure RTL flip-flop chain is removed, and so are the parameters PARA_AFIFO_SYNC_USE_CELL and PARA_AFIFO_SYNC_STAGE: the number of stages S is set by the cell option PARA_AFIFO_CELL_TYPE (0, 2, 2, 3, 4). m_vlsit_afifo_wr, m_vlsit_afifo_rd, and m_vlsit_afifo_top keep only PARA_AFIFO_CELL_TYPE (default 2). The macro VLSIT_SYNTHESIS no longer selects anything in m_vlsit_afifo_sync. The default configuration therefore uses the example cell models until real library cells exist.

The example technology cell models are synthesizable RTL under the RTL rules, one module per file in the folder 000_Common/rtl_cells (VLSIT_CELL_SYNC_DFF_RN/SN, VLSIT_CELL_SYNC_2FF_RN/SN, VLSIT_CELL_SYNC_3FF_RN/SN, VLSIT_CELL_SYNC_4FF_RN/SN). Their pins follow the naming rule instead of a library pin style: i_clk_dst, i_rst_n_dst (RN) or i_set_n_dst (SN), i_d, o_q; the wrapper maps the pins of the real cell when it replaces them. The SRAM model VLSIT_CELL_SRAM_1W1R stays simulation-only.

The SRAM macro model VLSIT_CELL_SRAM_1W1R is synthesizable RTL (one module, file 000_Common/rtl_cells/VLSIT_CELL_SRAM_1W1R.sv, parameters ADDR_W and DATA_W, bit write mask BWEB, read data register QR, no reset). Its module name, parameter names, and pin names CLKW, WEB, AW, DW, BWEB, CLKR, REB, AR, QR keep the library-macro style and are exempt from the naming rule; all other rules apply. A read of the address written at the same edge returns the old word; the simulation branch of the wrapper still returns X there.

The example cell models of DEC-040 (VLSIT_CELL_SYNC_*) keep the usual pin names of a library cell, CK, RN or SN, D, Q, and are exempt from the naming rule for module and pin names, like the SRAM macro model (DEC-041); all other rules apply. This replaces the pin names i_clk_dst, i_rst_n_dst, i_set_n_dst, i_d, o_q of DEC-040.

m_vlsit_afifo_ram_macro only instantiates VLSIT_CELL_SRAM_1W1R. Its simulation branch (behavioral model returning X on a read-write collision) is removed, so the macro model of DEC-041 is used in simulation and in synthesis, and a read of an address written at the same edge returns the old word. The macro VLSIT_SYNTHESIS selects branches only in m_vlsit_afifo_cell_sync.

The wrapper modules m_vlsit_afifo_cell_sync and m_vlsit_afifo_ram_macro are in the folder rtl_lib, separate from the FIFO logic in rtl; the example cells and the macro model stay in 000_Common/rtl_cells. Each folder has its own filelist.f.

The port lists of all RTL modules are aligned in four columns (direction, type, width, name) and declared in functional groups with a comment per group, clock and reset first (REF-003 FIL-05, FIL-06; skill rules R-030, R-031). The earlier grouping by direction (HIE-03) is replaced. The groups of the top are write clock and reset, write interface, software reset, read clock and reset, read interface.

The folders rtl_lib and rtl_cells are moved to common_rtl/000_Common. Library wrappers, cells, and macro models of this and of every later IP are written in 000_Common, not in the folder of the IP. This replaces the location in DEC-044; the content and the roles are unchanged.

The cell and macro models follow the skill rule R-032: the module name is VLSIT_CELL_, and the header states that the model is synthesizable RTL and that a real design uses the cell of the synthesis library. The models of this IP are renamed EX_SYNC_* to VLSIT_CELL_SYNC_* and EX_SRAM_1W1R to VLSIT_CELL_SRAM_1W1R; pin and parameter names keep the library style (DEC-041, DEC-042). Where an earlier decision names a model by its old name, the new name applies. The basic cells (gates, multiplexers, flip-flops, latches, clock cells) are delivered in the same folder 000_Common/rtl_cells.
